sources: GOV.UK Search & Content API (HMRC, HM Treasury, Companies House, The Pensions Regulator)

items.title: Check if a business is registered for money laundering supervision
items.description: Find out if a business has registered with HMRC under the money laundering regulations and report them if they have not.
items.changeNote: The Supervised Business Register has been updated.

ai.summary: The Supervised Business Register lists businesses registered with HMRC for money‑laundering supervision. Use it to confirm a counterpart’s status; if absent, contact them and, if still unregistered, report the suspicion to HMRC. Registration provides AML guidance but is not an endorsement.
ai.whoAffected: SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and self‑employed who need to verify AML supervision of counterparties and businesses that must be supervised under the money‑laundering regulations
actions: Search the Supervised Business Register to confirm a business’s registration number and details
If the business is not listed, contact it directly to verify its registration status
Advise any unregistered business to apply for supervision with HMRC
Report a suspected unregistered business to HMRC as tax fraud or avoidance

items.title: Edition 8: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax — software developer newsletter
items.description: HMRC's newsletter for software developers for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax.

ai.summary: HMRC’s newsletter updates software developers on Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, covering changes, service performance and required developer actions. Next edition due November 2026.
ai.whoAffected: Software developers building Making Tax Digital for Income Tax solutions
actions: Monitor HMRC’s newsletter for updates
Review any developer action items communicated
Plan for the next edition release in November 2026
Inform clients of any software changes that may affect them

items.title: Inheritance Tax: application for a clearance certificate (IHT30)
items.description: Use form IHT30 to apply for a clearance certificate, showing you have paid all the Inheritance Tax due.
items.changeNote: The formatting in the section "Date of amendments to the account" has been updated in the IHT30 form.

ai.summary: Use form IHT30 to apply for a clearance certificate once you are sure all inheritance tax has been paid, and you can request the form in Welsh by emailing HMRC.
ai.whoAffected: Anyone (e.g., personal representatives or executors) needing a clearance certificate to confirm inheritance tax is fully paid
actions: Confirm that all inheritance tax due has been paid
Email HMRC to request the IHT30 form (or a Welsh version)
Complete the IHT30 form with the required details
Submit the completed form to HMRC for the clearance certificate

items.title: Fulfilment House Due Diligence Scheme registered businesses list
items.description: Check if the business that stores your goods in the UK is registered with the Fulfilment House Due Diligence Scheme if you’re a trader based outside of the UK.
items.changeNote: The list has been updated with 23 additions, 2 amendments and 7 removals.

ai.summary: Use the list to confirm if a UK‑based fulfilment house storing your overseas client’s goods is registered under the Fulfilment House Due Diligence Scheme.
ai.whoAffected: Traders not established in the UK who store goods in the UK
actions: Identify overseas clients who use UK fulfilment houses
Check the HMRC list to see if the fulfilment house is registered
If the house is not on the list, advise the client to contact VAT enquiries or email notificationofnoncompliance.fulfilmenthouse@hmrc.gov.uk
Record the verification outcome for client files

items.title: Refunds of UK VAT for non-UK businesses (VAT Notice 723A)
items.description: How to claim a VAT refund in the UK if you're established outside the UK.
items.changeNote: Information about submitting an electronic claim for a VAT refund has been updated at section 2.10.

ai.summary: The notice sets out how non‑UK businesses can reclaim UK VAT they’ve paid on imports or UK purchases, provided they’re not UK‑VAT registered and meet residency conditions. Claims must be filed electronically or by post by 31 December of the prescribed year, with supporting documents retained.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses established outside the UK (including EU firms) that incur UK VAT and are not registered, liable or eligible for UK VAT, and have no UK place of business or supplies (except limited transport services).
actions: Confirm client meets eligibility – not UK‑VAT registered, no UK residence or supplies, and their home country offers reciprocal relief
Collect required documents: completed VAT65A form, certificate of status, original invoices and any supporting evidence
Submit the claim electronically via HMRC’s Transfer Files service before 31 December of the prescribed year, keeping all original documents
If no receipt or response within 6 months, email the Overseas Repayment Unit (ORU) with the receipt and retain proof of postage for postal claims
legislationRefs: Value Added Tax Regulations 1995 (SI 1995/2518) Parts 20A and XXI
Schedule 9 to the Value Added Tax Act 1994

items.title: Prohibition of promotion of certain tax avoidance arrangements
items.description: HMRC guidance on sections 159 to 165 of the Finance Act 2026 to introduce new rules that prohibit the promotion of certain tax avoidance arrangements (POP).

ai.summary: Guidance outlines rules that ban promoting certain tax avoidance schemes under sections 159‑165 of the Finance Act 2026.
ai.whoAffected: Not stated in source
actions: Not stated in source
legislationRefs: sections 159 to 165 of the Finance Act 2026

items.title: Reporting fund — annual report (CISC2)
items.description: Use form CISC2 to report your approved annual offshore funds to HMRC.
items.changeNote: Information on what to include in the 'Share Class details' section on page 4 of the form has been updated.

ai.summary: Use form CISC2 to submit the annual report for offshore funds approved as reporting funds, downloading the form, opening it in the latest free Adobe Reader, completing it on-screen, and contacting support if it won’t open.
ai.whoAffected: Owners or managers of offshore funds that have been approved as reporting funds
actions: Email HMRC to request a Welsh version of the form if required
Download and save the CISC2 form to your computer
Open the form using the latest free version of Adobe Reader and complete it on-screen
If the form won’t open, contact online services support for assistance

items.title: HMRC email updates, videos and webinars for tax agents and advisers
items.description: Learn more about the support available to tax agents and advisers which will help you and your clients.
items.changeNote: Recorded webinars for 'Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) overview' and 'VAT on private school fees' have been added. Recorded webinar links for 'Tackling criminal activity within the waste industry' and 'Labour supply chains featuring umbrella companies' have been updated. The live webinar for 'How to pay Vaping Products Duty and use the Vaping Duty Stamps scheme' has been replaced with a recorded webinar. The recorded webinar for 'The reduced rate of VAT during the children's summer holidays 2026' has been removed.

ai.summary: HMRC provides email updates and a range of live and recorded webinars covering Making Tax Digital for Income Tax, Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, multi‑factor authentication, OECD Pillar 2, Theatre Tax Relief, capital allowances and compliance standards, helping agents advise SME, owner‑managed and self‑employed clients.
ai.whoAffected: Tax agents and advisers and the SME, owner‑managed and self‑employed clients they support
actions: Subscribe to the HMRC help and support email service
Register for live webinars relevant to client needs
Watch recorded webinars to stay current on MDIT, CBAM, Pillar 2 and other topics
Use the guidance to prepare client authorisations and compliance processes
legislationRefs: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
Capital allowances — full expensing and 50% first year allowances

items.title: Personal Tax: Offshore Anti-Avoidance external engagement
items.description: The government will adopt a co-creation approach involving a small group of external expert alongside wider stakeholder engagement to help shape reform.
items.changeNote: Included an update on external engagement.

ai.summary: The government will use a co‑creation approach, inviting representative bodies and wider stakeholders to help design new policy and modernised legislation for Personal Tax Offshore Anti‑Avoidance, with periodic updates posted online.
ai.whoAffected: Not stated in source
actions: Monitor the HMRC engagement page for updates on the offshore anti‑avoidance review
Determine if your practice could be invited as a representative body and express interest
Prepare to contribute to policy design discussions if invited
Inform clients that reforms are being considered and may affect offshore arrangements
legislationRefs: Personal Tax Offshore Anti Avoidance legislation

items.title: Tell HMRC you want to claim Research and Development (R&D) tax relief
items.description: Check if you need to submit a claim notification form before you claim R&D Corporation Tax relief, what information you’ll need to provide and how to send it.
items.changeNote: Updated information to explain that you will no longer need to submit a claim notification form for Research and Development tax relief for claims made on or after 1 April 2027.

ai.summary: Companies claiming R&D tax relief must submit a claim notification form if it’s their first claim or their last claim was over three years ago, unless the claim is for periods starting on or after 1 April 2027, when the form is no longer required.
ai.whoAffected: UK companies (including SMEs and owner‑managed businesses) planning to claim R&D tax relief, especially first‑time claimants or those whose previous claim was more than three years ago
actions: Check whether the client needs to submit a claim notification form (first claim or last claim >3 years)
Calculate the claim notification period – from the start of the period of account to six months after its end
Collect required details: UTR, senior R&D contact, agent contacts, accounting‑period dates, period‑of‑account dates and a high‑level activity summary
Submit the form via Government Gateway within the period, save the confirmation reference and advise the client on next steps

items.title: Choose the right software for Pillar 2 Top-up Taxes
items.description: Find out what commercial software is available to report Domestic Top-up Tax and Multinational Top-up Tax.
items.changeNote: The list of Pillar 2 commercial software suppliers has been updated with one addition.

ai.summary: Domestic and Multinational Top‑up Taxes impose a 15% global minimum corporate tax on the largest groups, effective for accounting periods starting on or after 31 December 2023. HMRC does not endorse any software; agents must ensure they have Pillar 2 access.
ai.whoAffected: Largest corporate groups and any agents acting on behalf of those groups
ai.effectiveDate: Accounting periods beginning on or after 31 December 2023
actions: Confirm whether the client needs to report Pillar 2 Top‑up Taxes
Ensure you have Pillar 2 access as an agent if representing a client
Review available commercial software options (HMRC does not recommend any specific product)
Contact the chosen software provider for any technical issues

items.title: Amend a VAT group
items.description: Use form VAT50/51 to amend or remove an existing VAT group.
items.changeNote: New information added to explain how changes to VAT group membership can affect a business’s EORI number and customs activity.

ai.summary: Use form VAT50/51 to add, remove or disband a VAT group. Gather each member’s incorporation details, turnover, VAT number, exemption status and capital asset info, confirm control conditions, and consider EORI changes. Submit online (or paper) via an authorised signatory, adding VAT53 if an agent.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses that are part of a VAT group, including SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and self‑employed entities with a VAT registration
actions: Collect all required details for each existing or proposed group member (incorporation, turnover, VAT number, exemption status, capital assets, control conditions)
Complete and submit form VAT50/51 online or by post, ensuring it is signed by an authorised company director, secretary or group controller
If an employee, accountant or agent files the form, also provide a completed VAT53 form
Check EORI implications: cancel any EORI linked to the old group and apply for a new EORI if needed

items.title: Confirmation statement (CS01)
items.description: Use this form to confirm that the company's details are up to date.
items.changeNote: Edited section 'Restoring a company' to clarify that you need to file a paper confirmation statement (CS01) if you’re restoring a company to the register.

ai.summary: The CS01 form confirms a company’s details on the Companies House register. It can be filed online (cheaper) or on paper (£110). Use parts 1‑4 for changes to SIC, capital, share trading status, PSC and shareholders; part 5 for a registered email. Paper filing is required when restoring a company.
ai.whoAffected: All limited companies, including SMEs and owner‑managed businesses, that need to file a confirmation statement, especially those restoring a company to the register.
actions: Check if the client is restoring a company; if so, advise filing a paper CS01.
Gather and verify identity details for all current directors before completing the form.
Update any changes to SIC codes, capital, share trading status, PSC exemption, shareholder information and provide a registered email using the appropriate parts of the form.
Submit the completed form on full‑size A4 paper (or recommend online filing for non‑restoration cases) and ensure the correct confirmation date is used.

items.title: Draft legislation: Better use of new and improved third-party data
items.description: We welcome views on this technical consultation to improve the quality and consistency of data HMRC receives on interest income and card sales.

ai.summary: The consultation proposes new reporting duties for banks, building societies, merchant acquirers and payment facilitators to supply HMRC with interest income and card‑sales data, improving data matching and compliance, with obligations starting 6 April 2028.
ai.whoAffected: Banks, building societies, merchant acquirers, payment facilitators and other organisations that hold interest income or card‑sales data for customers.
actions: Check which of your clients are data‑holders (banks, building societies, merchant acquirers or payment facilitators) and confirm they fall within the new reporting scope.
Advise clients to collect and verify the correct tax reference for each customer before data submission.
Set up a schedule to report interest income and card‑sales data to HMRC at the required frequency and within the set timeframe.
Implement a process to notify HMRC before each reporting run and to make reasonable efforts to obtain any missing data.

items.title: Income Tax: changes to tax rates for property and savings income
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about the changes to property rates and savings rates for 2027 to 2028 tax year.

ai.summary: Property and savings income tax rates rise to 24% basic, 44% higher and 49% additional from 6 April 2027.
ai.whoAffected: Individuals with property rental income and savings interest, including owners of SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and the self‑employed.
actions: Inform affected clients of the new rates
Recalculate projected tax liabilities for 2027/28
Review timing of property and savings income for possible planning
Update tax software settings to reflect the new rates

items.title: Tax-free savings newsletter 24
items.description: October 2026 newsletter to update stakeholders on the latest news for tax-free savings.

ai.summary: HMRC newsletter outlines updates for ISA managers and Child Trust Fund providers, covering reduced Lifetime ISA withdrawal charges, Help to Save steps, cash ISA limit retention, First Time Buyer ISA, compliance and savings income tax rates.
ai.whoAffected: Individual Savings Account (ISA) managers, Child Trust Fund providers, and their clients
actions: Review the reduced Lifetime ISA withdrawal charge for first‑home purchases above the price cap
Update clients on the next steps for the Help to Save scheme
Confirm that the cash ISA limit will be retained from 6 April 2027
Advise on First Time Buyer ISA options and ensure ISA compliance

items.title: Pension schemes newsletter 186 — October 2026
items.description: Newsletter 186, published by HMRC in October 2026 to update stakeholders on the latest news for pension schemes.

ai.summary: HMRC’s Pension Schemes Services newsletter outlines recent updates including the Budget and Finance Bill 2026, surplus extraction tax regime, access for terminally ill, lifetime allowance abolition, two‑year rule on death benefits, guided retirement schemes, IHT technical amendments, DigiRAS delay, online refund tool, contact info, flexibility and registration stats.
ai.whoAffected: Stakeholders of pension schemes
actions: Review the Budget and Finance Bill 2026 implications for client pension schemes
Assess the impact of the surplus extraction tax regime and lifetime allowance abolition on client pensions
Advise clients on the delay of DigiRAS and the IHT technical amendments affecting pensions
Use the new online tool to claim pension tax refunds for clients
legislationRefs: Guided Retirement and Retirement Collective Money Purchase pension schemes

items.title: Reduce the main rate writing-down allowance and increase the main rate first-year allowance
items.description: This tax information and impact note covers the reduction of the main rate of writing-down allowances and the increase to the main rate first-year allowance.

ai.summary: From 2027 the main writing‑down allowance drops to 12% (CT 1 Apr, IT 6 Apr) and the main first‑year allowance rises to 50% for qualifying spend from 1 Jan 2027.
ai.whoAffected: Companies subject to Corporation Tax and individuals subject to Income Tax (including SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and the self‑employed)
ai.effectiveDate: Writing‑down allowance 12% from 1 Apr 2027 for Corporation Tax and 6 Apr 2027 for Income Tax; first‑year allowance 50% for expenditure incurred on or after 1 Jan 2027.
actions: Review client capital expenditure dates to apply the new 12% writing‑down rate and 50% first‑year rate
Adjust capital allowance calculations in upcoming tax returns
Advise clients on timing purchases to benefit from the higher first‑year allowance after 1 Jan 2027
Update practice software/templates with the new rates

items.title: VAT: supply of certain passenger transport services through agents
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about changes the VAT treatment of passenger transport services supplied by private hire vehicles or taxis through an agent.

ai.summary: From January 2028, VAT on taxi or private‑hire fares booked through an agent will be due from the agent, not the driver. VAT‑registered agents must charge VAT on the full fare, but only if the business’s turnover exceeds a set threshold.
ai.whoAffected: Taxi and private‑hire operators that use agents, and the agents themselves, where the business’s annual turnover is above the specified threshold
actions: Identify clients providing passenger transport services through agents
Check each client’s annual turnover against the threshold
If turnover exceeds the threshold, ensure the agent is VAT‑registered and charges VAT on the full fare
Update invoicing and accounting records to reflect the new VAT treatment

items.title: Machine Games Duty: changes to stake and prize thresholds
items.description: This tax information and impact note explains changes to the stake and prize thresholds used to determine whether a machine is a type 2 or type 3 machine for Machine Games Duty.

ai.summary: From 1 April 2027, machines charging over £1 or offering prizes over £100 will move from the standard 20% Machine Games Duty to a higher 25% rate.
ai.whoAffected: Owners of dutiable gaming machines (SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and self‑employed operators of such machines)
actions: Check each client’s gaming machines to see if the charge to play exceeds £1 or the prize exceeds £100
Recalculate Machine Games Duty at the 25% rate for any machines that meet the new thresholds
Advise clients on possible pricing or prize adjustments to remain at the 20% standard rate if desired
Update accounting records and future duty returns to reflect the higher rate from April 2027

items.title: Capital Gains Tax: reduction in the Business Asset Disposal Relief lifetime limit
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about the reduction in the Business Asset Disposal Relief lifetime limit.

ai.summary: Business Asset Disposal Relief lifetime limit cuts from £1 million to £500 thousand for qualifying disposals from 6 April 2027.
ai.whoAffected: SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and self‑employed individuals who would claim Business Asset Disposal Relief
actions: Review client eligibility for Business Asset Disposal Relief
Re‑calculate potential relief amounts using the new £500,000 limit
Advise clients on timing of asset disposals to maximise relief
Consider alternative reliefs or structuring options where the reduced limit impacts tax planning

items.title: Employment related securities bulletin 69 (October 2026)
items.description: Find out about the Budget 2026 changes to the Enterprise Management Incentive (EMI) and the Company Share Option Plan (CSOP) scheme, including rebranding CSOP as 'Enterprise Management Incentives 2 (EMI2)'.

ai.summary: From April 2027 the CSOP limit doubles to £120k, its options can run 15 years and no longer count towards EMI limits; CSOP is rebranded EMI2. EMI rules gain longer post‑disqualification exercise windows, EOT eligibility extension, and removal of separate grant notifications. BADR lifetime limit halves and securities transfer tax changes are delayed.
ai.whoAffected: Companies that run CSOP or EMI share‑option schemes and their employee shareholders, including SMEs and owner‑managed businesses using these incentives.
actions: Review client CSOP agreements to increase option values to £120,000 and extend exercise periods to 15 years, amending existing plans where possible
Inform clients that CSOP options no longer affect EMI individual limits and adjust EMI option modelling accordingly
Update EMI compliance: use the annual return for grant notification, note the extended 180‑day post‑disqualification window, and confirm EOT eligibility for upcoming transitions
Notify clients of the reduced BADR lifetime limit and upcoming securities transfer tax changes to plan for CGT impact and reporting responsibilities

items.title: Corporation Tax: CT620 Notes
items.description: These notes explain the different types of CT620 forms that HMRC may issue and why we send them.
items.changeNote: Information about CT620 AMD, AMK, ASA, CLA, CLO, COR, DET and DIS notices have been updated to explain why you may receive a notice, what your options are and when to make a payment. The 'Payment of tax' and 'Appeals' sections have also been updated with more information and links to relevant guidance.

ai.summary: The CT620 notes explain why HMRC sends a CT620 notice, what actions are required, payment timing (including group arrangements), handling of overpayments, options to appeal or postpone, and use of estimated figures.
ai.whoAffected: Companies that receive a CT620 notice, such as SMEs and owner‑managed businesses
actions: Determine the reason for the client’s CT620 notice
Check the payment deadline and arrange payment or a group payment plan
Advise on handling any overpayment of Corporation Tax
Assess whether to appeal or apply to postpone the payment

items.title: Stamp Duty Land Tax relief for land or property transactions
items.description: Find out what the main Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) reliefs are for land or property transactions.
items.changeNote: Information about Local Government Pension Scheme relief and how to claim it has been added.

ai.summary: The guidance outlines SDLT reliefs – first‑time buyer, shared‑ownership, multiple‑dwellings (ended 1 June 2024), building‑company, employer‑employee, compulsory purchase, planning‑obligation, group and seeding reliefs – and the relief codes to use on the SDLT return.
ai.whoAffected: First‑time home buyers, shared‑ownership buyers, purchasers of multiple dwellings, building companies buying homes, employers buying employee homes, local authorities or bodies making compulsory purchases, property developers with planning obligations, companies within the same group, and investment funds eligible for seeding relief.
actions: Identify which relief may apply to the client’s transaction and confirm eligibility criteria listed in the guidance
Enter the correct relief code (e.g., 32, 33, 08, 09, 10, 11, 12) on box 9 of the SDLT return
Keep supporting documentation to demonstrate eligibility and avoid penalties for incorrect claims
Advise the client on any limits (e.g., property value, land size, dates) that affect the relief

items.title: Zero rating medicines supplied free of charge (VAT Notice 1004)
items.description: Find out when you can zero-rate medicines supplied free of charge, including medicines for NHS treatment, clinical trials and continued treatment after a clinical trial.

ai.summary: Medicines supplied free of charge to the NHS, in clinical trials or for post‑trial treatment are zero‑rated for VAT from 23 June 2026, provided they meet authorisation and certificate requirements; otherwise they remain standard rated.
ai.whoAffected: Pharmaceutical companies supplying free medicines for NHS treatment, sponsors of clinical trials, companies participating in the Early Access to Medicines Scheme, importers/distributors of such medicines, and any business receiving free‑of‑charge medicines for qualifying uses.
actions: Check whether the client supplies medicines free of charge for NHS use, a clinical trial, or post‑trial treatment and confirm the product meets the authorisation criteria.
Verify the supply meets one of the qualifying conditions (marketing authorisation, regulation 167, or Early Access scheme).
Obtain and retain a valid certificate for each zero‑rated supply or import as required by the notice.
If VAT was charged on supplies between 23 June 2026 and 27 October 2026, advise the client to correct the VAT accounting.
legislationRefs: Medicines for Human Use (Clinical Trials) Regulations 2004
Schedule 9, Group 7 of the VAT Act 1994
Health and Social Care (Reform) Act (Northern Ireland) 2009
Health and Personal Social Services (Northern Ireland) Order 1991

items.title: Fuel and power (VAT Notice 701/19)
items.description: Find out what VAT should be charged on supplies of fuel and power if you're a supplier or a user.
items.changeNote: Information from Budget 2026 about an extension to the temporary zero rate has been added. Section 3.1.1 'Electric vehicle charging supplies' with guidance on new legislation has been added. Sections 2.3, 3.2.2, 3.3, 5.3, 10.1 and 10.7 have been updated with guidance related to this new legislation.

ai.summary: From 1 Oct 2026 to 30 Jun 2027 domestic electricity supplies in Great Britain are zero‑rated for VAT, while Northern Ireland continues at the 5% reduced rate. Qualifying use supplies receive the 0% rate; other supplies remain standard‑rated. The change affects both suppliers and end‑users of electricity.
ai.whoAffected: Suppliers of domestic electricity in England, Scotland and Wales, their business customers and residential users; Northern Ireland electricity suppliers (still 5% reduced rate); charities using electricity for non‑business purposes; any contractor invoicing for electricity‑related work must note the rate change.
actions: Confirm that the electricity you supply or purchase is for domestic qualifying use and apply 0% VAT during the temporary period
If you are a Northern Ireland supplier, continue to charge the 5% reduced rate on qualifying supplies
Review contracts and invoices to ensure reduced‑rate work is billed by the fuel‑or‑power supplier, not a third‑party contractor
Update accounting systems to automatically apply the correct VAT rate for the specified dates

items.title: Stamp Duty Land Tax on Leasehold sales
items.description: Find out about Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) on leasehold properties.
items.changeNote: From 1 May 2026, you do not need to work out the NPV of rent for a residential property under an assured tenancy.

ai.summary: From 1 May 2026 you no longer calculate NPV of rent for residential leases under an assured tenancy. SDLT on leasehold purchases is based on the premium and, where rent exceeds a nominal amount, the NPV of rent (except the above). Returns must be filed if the price is £40,000 or more, with specific exemptions.
ai.whoAffected: SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and self‑employed individuals buying or selling leasehold properties (new or assigned leases) in England and Northern Ireland
actions: Determine whether the lease is a new lease or an assigned lease and identify the premium and rent terms
Calculate SDLT on the premium using the same rates as for a freehold purchase
If rent is more than nominal and not an assured tenancy after 1 May 2026, compute the NPV of the rent and apply the 1% SDLT rate on any amount above the residential or non‑residential threshold
Submit an SDLT return online whenever the sale price is £40,000 or more, or when required by the specific lease‑duration and rent‑threshold exemptions

items.title: Conveyancers: Lifetime ISA technical guidance
items.description: Find out about first time residential purchases with funds from a Lifetime Individual Savings Account (ISA) if you're a conveyancer.
items.changeNote: From 29 October 2026, if funds are withdrawn to buy a property and the purchase price is more than £450,000 a 20% withdrawal charge will apply.

ai.summary: From 29 Oct 2026 a 20% charge applies when Lifetime ISA funds are withdrawn for a first‑time residential purchase over £450,000.
ai.whoAffected: Conveyancers handling first‑time residential purchases using Lifetime ISA funds
actions: Verify the purchase price exceeds £450,000
Calculate the 20% withdrawal charge if applicable
Inform the client of the charge before completing the transaction
Record the charge and update client files

items.title: Conveyancers: first time residential purchase with a Lifetime ISA
items.description: Find out about first time residential purchases with funds from a Lifetime Individual Savings Account (ISA) if you’re a conveyancer.
items.changeNote:
'Example of a model investor declaration' and 'Example of a model conveyancer declaration' have been updated.
From 29 October 2026, if funds are withdrawn to buy a property and the purchase price is more than £450,000 a 20% withdrawal charge will apply.

ai.summary: Conveyancers must ensure Lifetime ISA withdrawals for first‑time home purchases meet conditions, collect investor details, send required declarations to the ISA manager, and monitor the 90‑day completion rule, noting a 20% charge applies for properties over £450,000 from 29 Oct 2026.
ai.whoAffected: Conveyancers, their first‑time buyer clients using a Lifetime ISA, and ISA managers
ai.effectiveDate: From 6 April 2018 (original rules) and from 29 Oct 2026 (20% charge for purchases over £450,000)
actions: Collect all required investor information and verify eligibility criteria before withdrawal
Prepare and submit the model conveyancer declaration to the Lifetime ISA manager with required details
Track that the ISA manager releases funds within 30 days and ensure the purchase completes within 90 days
If the purchase fails or is delayed, notify the ISA manager within the specified timeframes and arrange any extensions or fund returns

items.title: Digital reporting for Lifetime ISAs
items.description: Find out the software requirements for reporting Lifetime ISA payments, transfers and withdrawals to HMRC.
items.changeNote: Added there is a 20% withdrawal charge if investors take money out of their Lifetime ISA for a first time residential property purchase and the property value is above £450,000.

ai.summary: LISA managers must digitally report all LISA activity via HMRC’s API, using authorised endpoints and OAuth tokens, including annual returns, bonuses, withdrawals and property purchases. Unmatched investor data causes failures; a 20% withdrawal charge applies for property buys over £450,000.
ai.whoAffected: LISA managers (including practice clients) and Lifetime ISA investors
actions: Integrate your practice software with HMRC’s LISA API and obtain OAuth 2.0 tokens
Test the integration in HMRC’s test environment before live use
Confirm investor personal details match HMRC records before creating investor records
Submit required annual returns and report any withdrawal charges, especially for property purchases above £450,000

items.title: Check employment related securities files
items.description: Use this service to check your files for formatting errors before submitting annual returns for employment related securities.
items.changeNote: Information has been added to confirm that Company Share Option Plans (CSOP) can also be known as Enterprise Management Incentives 2 (EMI2).

ai.summary: Employers and agents must use the ERS checking service to validate .ods or .csv files before filing annual ERS returns (including nil returns) by 6 July after the tax year ends, to avoid rejection and penalties.
ai.whoAffected: Employers and their agents who need to submit ERS annual returns, including SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and self‑employed employers
actions: Download the appropriate ERS spreadsheet template or create one using the technical notes
Populate the spreadsheet with scheme data and save as .ods or .csv
Run the file through the ERS checking service using a Government Gateway ID
Correct any errors identified, then submit the annual (or nil) return by 6 July

items.title: Late registrations for employment related securities
items.description: What to do if you miss the registration deadline for employment related securities.
items.changeNote: Information has been added to confirm that Company Share Option Plans (CSOP) can also be known as Enterprise Management Incentives 2 (EMI2).

ai.summary: Missing the registration deadline for employment related securities can forfeit tax benefits. Contact HMRC in writing, explain the reason, and if a reasonable excuse is accepted, follow their steps to register late and submit any overdue returns, noting possible penalties.
ai.whoAffected: Employers who run EMI, CSOP (EMI2), Save As You Earn, or Share Incentive Plan schemes and their employees
actions: Advise client to write to HMRC (email or post) explaining why the registration deadline was missed
If HMRC accepts a reasonable excuse, help client prepare and submit the late scheme registration and any required returns
Assist with using HMRC’s secure file transfer service for late returns if required
Inform client of possible late filing penalties and guide them on how to appeal

items.title: How employment related securities work if you're an employer
items.description: Use employment related securities (ERS) to reward, retain or give incentives to your employees, including any tax advantages.
items.changeNote: Information has been added to confirm that Company Share Option Plans (CSOP) can also be known as Enterprise Management Incentives 2 (EMI2).

items.title: Stamp Duty Land Tax — Local Government Pension Scheme Relief
items.description: This measure is about changes to Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) for purchases made by Local Government Pension Scheme pooled investment vehicles.
items.changeNote: New guidance has been added about Stamp Duty Land Tax relief for transfers of land and property from Local Government Pension Scheme Administering Authorities to qualifying pooled investment vehicles, and the exchequer impact table has been updated for Budget 2026.

ai.summary: A temporary SDLT relief for LGPS pooled investment vehicles buying land/property from LGPS authorities, effective from Budget Day 2026 until 31 March 2032.
ai.whoAffected: Local Government Pension Scheme pooled investment vehicles and the LGPS administering authorities that sell land or property
actions: Confirm the client is a LGPS pooled investment vehicle
Verify the purchase date falls between Budget Day 2026 and 31 March 2032
Apply the SDLT relief when calculating duty due
Keep documentation of the relief claim for HMRC records

items.title: Capital gains: preventing protected cell company avoidance
items.description: This measure affects UK resident individuals, trustees and companies who hold assets through a non-UK resident protected cell company.

ai.summary: The rules for capital gains on assets held through non‑UK resident protected cell companies are changed, affecting gains attributed to UK resident individuals, trusts and companies, effective 28 Oct 2026.
ai.whoAffected: UK resident individuals, trusts and companies that hold assets via a non‑UK resident protected cell company
actions: Identify clients with assets held through non‑UK resident protected cell companies
Review their capital gains exposure under the new attribution rules
Advise on any reporting or tax liability implications
Update client records and monitor for further guidance

items.title: Capital Gains Tax relief on gifts of business assets
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about reforms to UK law relating to Capital Gains Tax relief for gifts of business assets.
items.changeNote: The equalities impacts information and exchequer impact table have been updated for Budget 2026.

ai.summary: The measure outlines new rules for Capital Gains Tax relief when business assets are gifted.
ai.whoAffected: Not stated in source

items.title: VAT: electronic invoicing
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about the introduction of e-invoicing requirements for VAT invoices (including public bodies) from April 2029.

ai.summary: From April 2029 VAT invoices must be issued electronically. HMRC will set detailed rules in future regulations or a notice and will act as the UK Peppol Authority, using Peppol as the core framework for e‑invoicing.
ai.whoAffected: All VAT‑registered businesses, including SMEs, owner‑managed firms, the self‑employed and public bodies that issue VAT invoices
actions: Monitor forthcoming regulations or HMRC notice for detailed technical requirements
Check that clients' invoicing software can generate Peppol‑compatible e‑invoices
Advise clients to plan migration to e‑invoicing before the April 2029 deadline
Consider recommending Peppol‑enabled solutions to ensure compliance

items.title: Securities Transfer Tax — modernisation of the Stamp Taxes on Shares Framework
items.description: The measure is about the Securities Transfer Tax that will apply on the transfer of securities and replace Stamp Duty and Stamp Duty Reserve Tax.
items.changeNote: Updated to confirm that Securities Transfer Tax (STT) will commence in late 2027. The Exchequer impact and economic impact have been updated, along with information about the impact on individuals and businesses, including use of the new digital system for transfers outside CREST.

ai.summary: Stamp Duty and SDRT will be replaced by a single Securities Transfer Tax, a digital self‑assessed charge on securities transfers, starting in late 2027.
ai.whoAffected: Anyone who transfers securities, including individuals, companies and partnerships that hold or trade shares.
actions: Inform clients that Stamp Duty and SDRT will cease and a new digital STT will apply
Review clients' current share transfer processes and identify any upcoming transactions
Prepare clients for self‑assessment by setting up digital reporting mechanisms
Monitor HMRC guidance for detailed compliance requirements

items.title: Exploitation rights
items.description: This measure addresses the rights in relation to exploration and exploitation activities in the UK Continental Shelf.
items.changeNote: The effective date of this measure in respect of profits arising on or after 1 April 2027 for Corporation Tax purposes has changed. This measure will now have effect for accounting periods beginning on or after 13 July 2026 for Corporation Tax and for profits arising from 6 April 2027 for Income Tax.

ai.summary: The measure aligns UK double taxation agreements and ensures profits from rights to extract UK natural resources are taxed in the UK, with new effective dates for Corporation Tax and Income Tax.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses and individuals holding exploitation rights to UK natural resources, and any clients affected by double taxation agreements.
ai.effectiveDate: Accounting periods beginning on or after 13 July 2026 for Corporation Tax; profits arising on or after 1 April 2027 (Corporation Tax) and 6 April 2027 (Income Tax).
actions: Check client contracts for exploitation rights and note the new tax start dates
Update corporation tax filing schedules to reflect the 13 July 2026 start for affected periods
Advise clients on double‑tax treaty implications for UK resource profits
Ensure income‑tax calculations incorporate the 6 April 2027 effective date

items.title: Introduction of the Side-by-Side package and amendments to Multinational Top-up Tax and Domestic Top-up Tax
items.description: This measure is about the UK implementation of the Side-by-Side package and amendments being made to Multinational Top-up Tax and Domestic Top-up Tax.
items.changeNote: Information about the Side-by-Side package operative date and amendments made to Schedules 14 to 18 of the Finance (No.2) Act 2023 have been added for Budget 2026.

ai.summary: The measure brings the OECD Side‑by‑Side package into UK law and amends Multinational and Domestic Top‑up Tax to align with OECD and Inclusive Framework guidance.
ai.whoAffected: Entities subject to Multinational Top‑up Tax and Domestic Top‑up Tax
actions: Identify clients affected by Multinational or Domestic Top‑up Tax
Review the OECD Side‑by‑Side guidance published January 2026
Assess how the amendments change client tax positions
Update advice and planning to reflect the new UK legislation

items.title: Publishing details of deliberate defaulters reform
items.description: This measure is about changes to the publishing details of deliberate defaulters policy.
items.changeNote: This measure has been updated as the publication threshold increase to £50,000 was made by Statutory Instrument laid on 11 September 2026 and came into force on 2 October 2026.

ai.summary: The measure lets HMRC publish more information on deliberate non‑compliance and Personal Liability Notices, expanding the details shown for deliberate defaulters.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses identified as deliberate defaulters and individuals receiving Personal Liability Notices
actions: Review client compliance to prevent deliberate defaulter status
Advise clients on record‑keeping to reduce risk of Personal Liability Notices
Monitor HMRC publications for any client mentions
Prepare a response plan if a client is listed

items.title: Modernising the correction of errors
items.description: This measure introduces draft legislation on new requirements to correct inaccuracies in returns and documents provided to HMRC.
items.changeNote: This legislation becomes operative on 1 April 2028. The section ‘policy objective’ has been updated to confirm we will use assessment and penalty provisions in an aim to improve compliance. The ‘current law’ section has been updated with more information. ‘Proposed revisions’ has been updated with more detail about the legislation. The update in section ‘Impact on individuals, households and families’ and in section ‘Administrative impact on business including civil society organisations’ confirms there is an explicit obligation on taxpayers to correct errors once they are identified.

ai.summary: New legislation requires all taxpayers to correct any identified errors in returns or documents to HMRC, and gives HMRC power to issue a customer correction notice.
ai.whoAffected: All taxpayers, including SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and the self‑employed
actions: Check client returns and filings for any inaccuracies
Advise clients to promptly correct any identified errors
Prepare and submit correction notices to HMRC where required
Maintain records of corrections and correspondence with HMRC

items.title: Cryptoasset loans and liquidity pools
items.description: This measure is about the treatment of certain disposals involving cryptoasset loans and liquidity pools for Capital Gains Tax.
items.changeNote: Information about Exchequer impact and how Single Cryptoasset Lending Arrangements are treated have been updated.

ai.summary: The measure defers Capital Gains Tax on cryptoassets until an economic disposal, applying to single cryptoasset lending, borrowing, and automated market making arrangements.
ai.whoAffected: Taxpayers with cryptoasset lending, borrowing or automated market making arrangements, including SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and the self‑employed who hold cryptoassets.
actions: Identify clients with the listed cryptoasset arrangements
Determine if the deferral conditions are met for each client
Ensure clients keep records of any economic disposal of the cryptoasset
Direct any client queries to digitalassets@hmrc.gov.uk

items.title: Changes to reporting of benefits in kind from April 2027
items.description: This measure is about the changes to the reporting of certain benefits in kind from April 2027.
items.changeNote: Information about the background to this measure, the operative dates, proposed revisions, Exchequer impact, impact on individuals, households and families, equalities impacts, and administrative impacts has been updated.

ai.summary: From April 2027 benefits in kind like company cars, fuel and medical benefits must be reported via payroll software in real time, with a penalty easement for the first year; further benefits follow in April 2028.
ai.whoAffected: Employers providing company cars, car fuel, vans, van fuel, employer‑provided medical benefits and, later, other benefits in kind.
ai.effectiveDate: April 2027 (mandatory payrolling for listed benefits); April 2028 (extends to most remaining benefits).
actions: Check that client payroll software supports Real Time Information (RTI) for BIK reporting
Update client payroll processes to capture company car, fuel and medical benefit data each pay run
Advise clients of the temporary penalty easement and stress accuracy checks during the first year
Prepare for the April 2028 expansion by identifying other BIKs that will become subject to mandatory payrolling

items.title: Lifetime ISA withdrawal charge
items.description: This tax information and impact note explains the reduced Lifetime ISA withdrawal charge for first-time buyers purchasing a property above the property price cap.

ai.summary: From 29 Oct 2026, relevant Lifetime ISA withdrawals will let savers keep their own contributions but lose the government bonus; unauthorised withdrawals still incur a 25% charge.
ai.whoAffected: Savers with a Lifetime ISA making a relevant withdrawal after 29 Oct 2026
actions: Check whether a client’s withdrawal is a relevant Lifetime ISA withdrawal after the effective date
Explain that contributions can be retained but the government bonus will be removed
Confirm that any unauthorised withdrawal will still attract a 25% charge
Record the change in the client’s file and advise on tax implications

items.title: Reform of the foreign permanent establishment exemption
items.description: This measure reforms the taxation of foreign permanent establishments, making the elective exemption regime that applies to their profits and losses mandatory for Corporation Tax.
items.changeNote: Information about the Exchequer impact has been updated.

ai.summary: The measure makes the elective exemption for profits and losses of foreign permanent establishments mandatory for UK Corporation Tax.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses with foreign permanent establishments that are subject to Corporation Tax
actions: Identify clients with foreign permanent establishments
Inform them that the exemption will become mandatory for Corporation Tax
Adjust tax planning and filing to reflect the mandatory exemption
If appropriate, submit a consultation response to foreignpepolicy@hmrc.gov.uk by 13 September 2026

items.title: Changes to employee share schemes, including Company Share Option Plan and Enterprise Management Incentives
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about changes to the rules for employee share schemes.

ai.summary: From 6 April 2027 the CSOP and EMI schemes will see higher option limits, longer exercise periods, broader exceptions from disguised remuneration rules, and extended EMI exercise windows after disqualifying events.
ai.whoAffected: Employers offering CSOP or EMI share schemes, including SMEs and owner‑managed businesses, and their employee participants.
actions: Review current CSOP option limits and adjust to the increased individual limit
Update EMI documentation to reflect removal of interaction with CSOP limits and the extended exercise window after disqualifying events
Amend share option agreements to incorporate the longer CSOP exercise period and expanded disguised remuneration exceptions
Advise clients on the extended Employee Ownership Trusts exception within EMI rules

items.title: VAT changes following the abolition of NHS England
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about changes to the VAT Act 1994 which are required because NHS England will be abolished in 2027.

ai.summary: Amendments will be made to Groups 12 and 15 of Schedule 8 VAT Act 1994 when NHS England is abolished in 2027, preserving existing VAT treatment and removing NHS England references.
ai.whoAffected: Not stated in source
actions: Review client VAT positions under Groups 12 and 15 of Schedule 8 VAT Act 1994
Monitor the 2027 abolition of NHS England for any VAT changes
Update VAT records to remove references to NHS England
Advise clients on any impact to their VAT treatment
legislationRefs: Groups 12 and 15 of Schedule 8 VAT Act 1994

items.title: Individual Savings Accounts (ISAs) compliance package
items.description: The measure introduces a modern, fair and effective Individual Savings Account (ISA) compliance framework that supports digital reporting and makes sure the ISA system operates as intended.
items.changeNote: Information about the Exchequer impact has been updated.

ai.summary: A new ISA compliance framework requires managers to submit digital monthly and annual returns, introduces a points‑based penalty regime, allows HMRC to suspend managers, and lets HMRC collect tax and penalties for compliance failures.
ai.whoAffected: ISA managers and providers (including any SME or self‑employed clients that operate ISA schemes)
actions: Check that ISA‑manager clients have systems to file monthly and annual returns digitally
Implement checks to improve accuracy of returns to avoid points‑based penalties
Inform clients of the new suspension powers and prepare contingency plans
Advise clients on the updated ISA regulations and potential tax‑penalty calculations

items.title: Corporation Tax treatment of investment life insurance contract payouts
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about a change that clarifies when a company that is not a life insurance company can claim a partial Corporation Tax exemption on a payout from an investment life insurance contract.

items.title: Income Tax treatment of image rights payments connected to employment
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about the tax treatment of image rights payments connected to an employment.

ai.summary: All image rights payments linked to employment will be treated as taxable employment income, subject to Income Tax and NICs via PAYE from 6 April 2028.
ai.whoAffected: Employees receiving image‑rights payments and their employers, including SMEs and owner‑managed businesses that use such arrangements
actions: Review client contracts for any image‑rights payments
Inform clients that these payments will become taxable employment income via PAYE from 6 April 2028
Update payroll systems to treat image‑rights payments as earnings subject to Income Tax and NICs
Adjust tax planning and compliance advice to reflect the new treatment

items.title: Income Tax: changes resulting from new savings and property rates
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about changes to the savings and property rates of Income Tax.

ai.summary: From 6 April 2027 the basic rate for savings income rises and separate property income rates start; rules on insurers’ reporting, foreign life policy gains, deduction at source and Transfer of Assets Abroad are preserved.
ai.whoAffected: Insurers, holders of certain foreign life insurance policies, and taxpayers with savings or property income.
actions: Check client savings and property income to apply the new basic and separate rates from 6 April 2027
Confirm insurers’ reporting obligations remain unchanged for relevant clients
Verify that tax treatment of gains from foreign life policies continues as before
Review deduction‑at‑source and Transfer of Assets Abroad compliance for affected clients

items.title: High Value Council Tax Surcharge on residential properties
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about the High Value Council Tax Surcharge, a new annual charge on owners of residential property in England worth £2 million or above.

ai.summary: A new annual High Value Council Tax Surcharge applies from April 2028 to owners of English residential properties valued at £2 million or more, collected with Council Tax. Valuations will be targeted, with a deferral scheme, discounts, exemptions and a 100% premium on properties empty for 12 months.
ai.whoAffected: Owners of residential property in England worth £2 million or more, including those whose properties are empty for 12 months or longer
actions: Identify clients who own residential property in England valued at £2 million or above
Advise them on the upcoming valuation exercise and record keeping requirements
Explain the deferral scheme, available discounts and exemptions, and the 100% premium for long‑term empty properties
Prepare tax planning to incorporate the surcharge into cash‑flow forecasts

items.title: Tax treatment of stablecoins
items.description: This measure will treat eligible stablecoins more like money for tax purposes.
items.changeNote: Information about the taxation of eligible stablecoins for individuals, trustees and companies and deduction of sums representing Income Tax has been added, and the exchequer impact table has been updated for Budget 2026.

ai.summary: Eligible stablecoins are treated like money: individuals and trustees get CGT exemption on disposals and interest‑like returns are savings income; companies tax transactions based on amounts recorded in their accounts.
ai.whoAffected: Individuals, trustees and companies (including SMEs)
actions: Identify any eligible stablecoins held by clients and confirm their status
Record disposals for individuals/trustees as CGT‑exempt
Classify interest‑like returns from stablecoins as savings income for individuals/trustees
Ensure corporate clients record stablecoin transactions in their accounts and compute tax accordingly

items.title: Remote Gaming Duty: changes to freeplays, prizes and tournaments
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about changes to the Remote Gaming Duty rules for restricted plays (commonly known as freeplays), prizes and tournaments.

ai.summary: Amends Finance Act 2014 to change how restricted plays, tournament participation and prize definitions are treated for Remote Gaming Duty, including exclusion of wins using another restricted play and treatment of returned payments. Changes start 1 April 2027.
ai.whoAffected: Remote gaming operators that calculate Remote Gaming Duty, including those offering restricted plays (freeplays), tournaments and prizes
actions: Review client calculations of Remote Gaming Duty profits to ensure restricted plays, especially wins using another restricted play, are excluded as required
Determine whether tournament participation now counts as a game of chance under the new rules
Re‑examine the definition of a prize and how returned gaming payments after interruptions are treated
Update Remote Gaming Duty returns and internal policies to reflect the changes effective 1 April 2027

items.title: Capital Gains Tax exit charges for temporarily migrated trusts
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about trusts that become UK resident when a trustee moves to the UK.

ai.summary: Trusts that become UK resident because a trustee moves to the UK can stay resident for up to one year without triggering the CGT exit charge.
ai.whoAffected: Trusts that become UK resident due to a trustee moving to the UK and their trustees
actions: Identify any client trusts where a trustee has relocated to the UK
Confirm the trust meets the relief condition (resident because of the trustee move)
Advise the trust can remain UK resident for up to 12 months to avoid the CGT exit charge
Record the trustee’s move and track the one‑year residency period

items.title: Income Tax: assessing and collecting tax on lump sum death benefits above the allowance
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about changes to how Income Tax is charged on certain pension lump sum death benefits paid above the deceased member’s available lump sum and death benefit allowance.

items.title: Income Tax — withholding tax exemption for Scottish Government bonds
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about the removal of the obligation on the Scottish Government to apply withholding tax to certain interest payments.

items.title: Reverse charge on supplies received from abroad
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about changes to the business to business reverse charge for services supplied by overseas businesses to UK VAT registered recipients.

ai.summary: The B2B reverse charge now only applies when the UK buyer is VAT‑registered; if the buyer isn’t registered, the overseas supplier must charge and account for UK VAT.
ai.whoAffected: UK businesses receiving services from overseas suppliers, whether they are VAT‑registered or not
actions: Verify each client’s VAT registration status before applying the reverse charge
If a client is not VAT‑registered, advise that the overseas supplier must charge UK VAT
Adjust the client’s VAT accounting to remove the reverse charge for non‑registered clients
Notify overseas suppliers of the change in VAT treatment

items.title: Tax treatment of payments under the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero Electricity Bill Discount Scheme
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about a new Income Tax exemption for payments made under the Electricity Bill Discount Scheme.

ai.summary: Payments received under the Electricity Bill Discount Scheme are exempt from Income Tax from 6 April 2026.
ai.whoAffected: Anyone receiving payments under the Electricity Bill Discount Scheme, including community groups and potentially SME or self‑employed participants.
actions: Identify clients who receive Electricity Bill Discount Scheme payments
Confirm the exemption applies to those payments from 6 April 2026
Adjust clients' Income Tax calculations to remove the payments from taxable income
Maintain documentation showing the exemption for future HMRC queries

items.title: Increase in the banking surcharge rate for a temporary period
items.description: This tax information and impact note sets out the rate of surcharge on banking companies.

ai.summary: The surcharge rate on banking companies is set at 6% for a fixed 15‑month period, starting 1 January 2027.
ai.whoAffected: Banking companies
actions: Record the temporary 6% surcharge rate in client files
Update any advice that references banking fees to reflect the new rate
Monitor the 15‑month period for any further changes
Inform clients with banking relationships of the start date

items.title: VAT: removal of the exemption for a deputy for a medical practitioner
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about the removal of the VAT exemption for a deputy for a medical practitioner.

ai.summary: From 1 May 2027 the VAT exemption for supplying a deputy to a registered medical practitioner ends; medical care remains exempt, but deputy services will be subject to VAT.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses that supply deputy services to registered medical practitioners
actions: Identify any client providing deputy services to registered medical practitioners
Advise them that VAT will apply from 1 May 2027
Ensure they are VAT‑registered or adjust pricing to include VAT
Update contracts and invoicing to reflect the change

items.title: VAT refund claims made using form VAT126
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about legislation that will allow powers and safeguards to be introduced for VAT refund claims made using form VAT126.

ai.summary: New powers and safeguards will apply to VAT refund claims using form VAT126 made by bodies not registered for VAT, treating them like claims by VAT‑registered entities under specific sections of the VAT Act 1994.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses and individuals that are not VAT‑registered but submit VAT refund claims using form VAT126
actions: Identify clients making VAT126 refund claims who are not VAT‑registered
Advise them that their claims will now be subject to the same powers and safeguards as VAT‑registered claims
Ensure claim documentation meets the standards applied to VAT‑registered bodies
Monitor any further guidance on implementation of the new powers
legislationRefs: sections 33(1) of the Value Added Tax Act 1994
section 33A(2) of the Value Added Tax Act 1994
section 33B(2) of the Value Added Tax Act 1994
section 33C(3) of the Value Added Tax Act 1994
section 33E(2) of the Value Added Tax Act 1994

items.title: Statutory reorganisations: general power
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about the creation of a general power to neutralise any tax consequences of a reorganisation of public sector bodies.

items.title: Income Tax: changes to the definition of serious ill health lump sums and medical evidence requirements
items.description: This tax information and impact note explains changes to the test for qualifying for a serious ill health lump sum and to the medical evidence that practitioners outside the UK can provide.

ai.summary: The test for a serious ill‑health lump‑sum is now based on a member expected to live less than 12 months, and overseas doctors can supply evidence if the member lives in the same country or the scheme is established there.
ai.whoAffected: Pension scheme members and the pension schemes they belong to, especially where members reside abroad or the scheme is set up outside the UK
actions: Check client pension scheme rules to see if any members may qualify under the new less‑than‑12‑months test
Update client advice to reflect the new eligibility criteria for serious ill‑health lump sums
Notify clients that medical evidence can now be provided by overseas practitioners when the member lives in the same country or the scheme is established there
Amend documentation templates to capture and verify overseas medical evidence and residency details

items.title: Stamp Duty Land Tax — changes to group relief
items.description: This measure is about changes to Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) where group relief has been claimed on a purchase of land or property.

ai.summary: A change of control test is added to SDLT group relief; if a company that claimed group relief later uses the winding‑up exception and its control changes within 3 years, relief is withdrawn and extra SDLT charged.
ai.whoAffected: Companies that have claimed SDLT group relief on land or property purchases and may later de‑group or experience a change of control, including SME owner‑managed groups.
actions: Review client transactions where group relief was claimed to spot any pending control changes within three years
Advise clients to manage or avoid ownership/control changes that could trigger the new test
Calculate potential additional SDLT if the winding‑up exception applies after a control change
Update client tax planning and documentation to reflect the withdrawal of group relief under the new rule

items.title: Changes to the Seed Enterprise Investment Scheme, Enterprise Investment Scheme and Venture Capital Trusts
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about changes to the Seed Enterprise Investment Scheme (SEIS), Enterprise Investment Scheme (EIS) and Venture Capital Trusts (VCT) scheme.

ai.summary: The rules for SEIS, EIS and VCT are updated: relief stays within scheme limits when limits are exceeded, same‑day investments are allowed, one investor’s late payment won’t affect others, interest‑charge rules are aligned, and VCT relief withdrawal uses the original rate.
ai.whoAffected: Investors in SEIS, EIS and VCT and companies raising finance through these schemes, including SME owners and their advisers
actions: Check client investment amounts against scheme limits and adjust relief calculations accordingly
Confirm that SEIS, EIS or VCT investments can be scheduled on the same day without affecting eligibility
Update client agreements to note that a late payment by one investor does not impact other investors' tax relief
Revise advice on interest charges and VCT relief withdrawal to reflect the aligned EIS rules

items.title: Inheritance Tax: preventing unintended deductions for liabilities in trust arrangements
items.description: This measure will amend the Inheritance Tax rules on liabilities relating to settled property to make sure they operate as intended and provide greater certainty about how liabilities are taken into account for Inheritance Tax purposes.

items.title: Income Tax: removing the pensions tax two-year rule
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about removing the two-year rule for tax-free pension and lump sum death benefits.

items.title: Capital Gains Tax — capital sums received for surrendering rights
items.description: This measure is about the surrender of rights under the terms of a contract.

ai.summary: Capital sums received for surrendering contractual rights are treated as capital gains and fall within Capital Gains Tax.
ai.whoAffected: Individuals and businesses that receive capital sums when they give up rights under a contract
actions: Identify clients receiving capital sums for surrendering rights
Confirm the receipt is subject to CGT
Include the amount in the client’s CGT calculation and reporting
Advise on record‑keeping and any available reliefs

items.title: VAT: introducing a new zero rate on donated medicines
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about introducing a new zero rate of VAT for qualifying donations of medicines.

items.title: Capital Gains Tax: returns for disposals of UK land and late filing penalties
items.description: This measure is about people who have disposed of an interest in UK residential property and have not reported the disposal on the correct return.

items.title: Company director disqualification following breach of HMRC securities legislation
items.description: This tax information and impact note explains changes that allow courts to consider director disqualification following a conviction for an offence under HMRC securities legislation.

items.title: Income Tax: increasing the trading allowance
items.description: This tax information and impact note details legislation introduced to increase the income tax trading allowance to £3,000, for trades and miscellaneous income.

ai.summary: The trading allowance rises from £1,000 to £3,000 for the 2027‑2028 tax year, also raising the self‑assessment reporting threshold to £3,000 for trade and miscellaneous income.
ai.whoAffected: Self‑employed individuals, SMEs and owner‑managed businesses with trading or miscellaneous income who file Income Tax self‑assessment
actions: Notify affected clients of the higher trading allowance and reporting threshold
Adjust tax calculations and self‑assessment forms to reflect the £3,000 allowance
Update practice software and templates with the new figures
Review whether clients should claim the allowance or opt for actual expense deduction

items.title: Stamp Duty Land Tax: assured tenancies
items.description: This measure changes the Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) treatment of rent payable under assured tenancies.

ai.summary: Rent payable under assured tenancies is no longer subject to SDLT and most reporting requirements are removed.
ai.whoAffected: Landlords of assured tenancies and their tenants, including SME landlords and self‑employed property owners
actions: Check client assured tenancy agreements to confirm they are covered by the new rules
Advise clients that SDLT is not payable on rent under assured tenancies
Remove SDLT reporting tasks from client compliance checklists
Notify affected clients of the change and update engagement letters

items.title: Updating the tax treatment of certain lease and leaseback arrangements
items.description: This measure is about a change that maintains the existing treatment of finance leaseback arrangements following changes to accounting standards.

items.title: National Savings and Investments tracing issue: tax treatment
items.description: This measure gives the Treasury a regulation-making power to introduce tax reliefs and administrative easements for holdings and payments affected by historic failures in National Savings & Investments (NS&I) tracing processes for bereavement claims.

ai.summary: The Treasury can grant tax reliefs and administrative easements for estates affected by historic NS&I tracing failures, exempting the holdings from Inheritance Tax and removing Income Tax on accrued interest, with compensation where appropriate.
ai.whoAffected: Estates of customers whose NS&I savings were not traced and paid after death due to historic failures.
ai.effectiveDate: From Royal Assent to the Finance Act 2027
actions: Identify clients with untraced NS&I accounts after death
Advise clients to claim the full value of holdings from NS&I
Prepare claims for Inheritance Tax exemption and Income Tax relief on accrued interest
Monitor secondary legislation for detailed reliefs and ensure compliance

items.title: Income Tax treatment of immigration skills charge and certificate of sponsorship fees
items.description: This measure will exempt employer paid immigration skills charge and certificate of sponsorship fees from Income Tax and Class 1a National Insurance contributions.

items.title: Enterprise Management Incentives (EMI): simplification of the process to grant options
items.description: This measure is about the removal of the requirement to submit a notification of a grant of Enterprise Management Incentives (EMI) options.
items.changeNote: From on or after 6 April 2027 changes apply to Enterprise Management Incentives (EMI) options granted. The 'Background to the measure' section has been updated to confirm the draft legislation about the EMI options was published for technical consultation on 13 July 2026 as part of Legislation Day. Changes to the EMI options have been added to the sections 'Proposed revisions' and 'Administrative impact on business including civil society organisations'. The exchequer impact table has been updated for Budget 2026.

items.title: VAT online marketplace liability extension
items.description: This tax information and impact note is about the extension of online marketplace liability to all sales of goods where the marketplace facilitates the sale of those goods by UK businesses.

ai.summary: VAT online marketplace rules now require marketplaces to collect VAT on sales by UK VAT‑registered businesses and other UK businesses with sales over £90,000 per platform, when goods are in the UK at sale. Personal, second‑hand and B2B sales are excluded.
ai.whoAffected: UK VAT‑registered businesses and other UK businesses exceeding the £90,000 per‑platform threshold, and the online marketplaces that facilitate those sales
actions: Check client sales on each marketplace to see if the £90,000 threshold is met
Advise clients that the marketplace must account for VAT on qualifying sales and adjust their VAT returns accordingly
Update client accounting systems to record VAT collected by the marketplace
Confirm that personal, second‑hand and B2B sales remain outside the new rules

items.title: Corporate Interest Restriction — interaction with creative reliefs
items.description: This measure makes technical changes to the Corporate Interest Restriction rules so they work as intended.

items.title: Income Tax: company car tax rates for 2030 to 2032
