ai.whoAffected: All users of the Find and update company information service, including SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and self‑employed who access Companies House services, especially those using shared company accounts
actions: Advise clients to create their own GOV.UK One Login linked to an individual email and phone
Review any shared Companies House accounts and plan separate individual accounts
Notify clients of the upcoming sign‑in change and the need for MFA setup
Ensure clients set up an authenticator app or SMS for multi‑factor authentication

items.title: Agent Update: issue 146
items.description: Get guidance from HMRC if you're a tax agent or an adviser

ai.summary: Agent Updates provide guidance for tax agents and advisers; the next edition is due September 2026 and covers tax, borders and trade, Making Tax Digital, HMRC services and agent engagement. Sign up for email alerts.
ai.whoAffected: Tax agents and advisers
actions: Review the current Agent Update for relevant guidance
Note that the next edition will be published in September 2026
Sign up for email reminders to receive future editions
Monitor the highlighted topics (tax, borders and trade, Making Tax Digital, HMRC services, agent engagement)

items.title: HMRC email updates, videos and webinars for employing people
items.description: Learn more about getting started as an employer or running a small business including registration, payroll, tax returns, tax bills and payments.
items.changeNote: Live webinars for 'Employees with more than one workplace', 'Employee travel', 'Phones, internet and homeworking' and 'Trivial benefits' have been added. The webinar links for 'Company cars, vans and fuel' and 'Labour supply chain due diligence for local authorities' have been updated.

ai.summary: HMRC offers email updates, videos and live/recorded webinars covering employer registration, payroll, tax codes, benefits, statutory pay and other obligations, helping new and existing employers manage taxes, reporting and compliance.
ai.whoAffected: Employers and small‑business owners, including owner‑managed businesses and self‑employed people who employ staff
actions: Subscribe to the HMRC help and support email service for updates
Register clients for relevant live webinars (e.g., employer filing obligations, payroll, trivial benefits)
Direct clients to the video collections for new‑employer guidance, tax codes and running a small business
Advise clients to use their HMRC business tax account to add and manage taxes such as PAYE, Corporation Tax, Self Assessment and VAT

items.title: Employer Bulletin: August 2026
items.description: A bi-monthly magazine for employers and agents that gives up-to-date information on payroll topics.

ai.summary: The August 2026 Employer Bulletin outlines guidance on making PAYE Settlement Agreement payments, the phased roll‑out of mandatory benefits‑in‑kind payrolling, consultations on lower‑value tax debts and aligning NI recovery limits with Income Tax, plus help for parent or carer employees to claim Child Benefit.
ai.whoAffected: Employers, payroll agents and employees who are parents or carers
actions: Advise clients to ensure their PAYE Settlement Agreement payment is made as required
Prepare clients for the upcoming mandatory payrolling of benefits in kind by reviewing current processes
Monitor the government consultations on low‑value tax debts and NI recovery time limits and inform clients of any changes
Assist client employees who are parents or carers in claiming their entitled Child Benefit

items.title: Order certified documents and certificates from Companies House
items.description: How to order certified copies of certificates and documents held on the Companies House register.
items.changeNote: The message about being unable to process requests for company certificates until further notice has been removed. The issue has been resolved.

ai.summary: Companies House lets you order certified company certificates or document copies via its online service or phone, with standard (£22) or express (£65) dispatch. You can add extra facts, but not PSC or share details. Legalisation is possible through the FCDO for Hague Convention countries.
ai.whoAffected: SMEs, owner‑managed companies and their advisers who need certified copies or certificates from Companies House
actions: Advise clients to order certificates or copies using the Find and update service or call 0303 1234 500
Recommend choosing standard or express dispatch, noting costs and timelines, and checking for postal delays
Ensure clients request any additional certified facts needed, remembering restrictions on PSC, shareholders and capital statements
If a document is needed abroad, guide clients to legalise it through the FCDO, confirming it has a British official’s original signature

items.title: Extend Child Benefit for your teen before 31 August
items.description: Parents have until 31 August to extend Child Benefit for their 16 to 19-year-olds who are continuing in non-advanced approved education or training.

ai.summary: Parents must extend Child Benefit for 16‑19‑year‑olds in non‑advanced education by 31 August 2026 or payments stop; can be done online, by post or phone; check HICBC liability if income exceeds £60,000.
ai.whoAffected: Parents of 16‑ to 19‑year‑old children who are continuing in non‑advanced approved education or training, including self‑employed parents
actions: Identify clients with 16‑19‑year‑old children in approved education and confirm they have extended their claim
Advise clients to extend the claim via the HMRC app or GOV.UK before the 31 August deadline
If digital access is unavailable, guide clients to use the post or phone method detailed in their HMRC letter
Remind clients with an individual adjusted net income over £60,000 to assess any High Income Child Benefit Charge using the online calculator

items.title: Apply for an exemption from Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
items.description: Find out how to apply for an exemption from Making Tax Digital for Income Tax.
items.changeNote: Information about 'When to apply' for an exemption if you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2027 has been updated.

ai.summary: Clients may be exempt from Making Tax Digital for Income Tax if they are digitally excluded or meet other criteria; they must apply to HMRC with personal details and reasons, and continue filing Self Assessment as normal.
ai.whoAffected: Self Assessment taxpayers, including self‑employed individuals and owners of SMEs who may need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
actions: Check whether the client is automatically exempt or needs to apply for an exemption
Collect the client’s NI number, address and a written explanation (including digital‑exclusion evidence if relevant)
Submit the application by calling or writing to HMRC using the correct subject line for the exemption type
If the application is refused, advise the client on the 30‑day appeal process and maintain normal Self Assessment record‑keeping

items.title: HMRC tools and calculators
items.description: Find and use tools and calculators that will help you work out your tax.
items.changeNote: A 'Deadlines' section has been added to help you find out the filing and payment deadlines for your taxes, and add them to your calendar.

ai.summary: HMRC provides an extensive suite of online tools and calculators covering duties, allowances, taxes, benefits and compliance checks, including a new Deadlines tool to help clients track filing and payment dates, useful for SMEs, owner‑managed firms and the self‑employed.
ai.whoAffected: SMEs, owner‑managed businesses, self‑employed individuals, partnerships, limited companies, directors, employees, trustees and anyone needing to calculate tax, duties or compliance obligations
actions: Identify which HMRC tools are relevant to each client’s situation and bookmark them
Use the new Deadlines tool to add filing and payment dates to the practice’s calendar
Guide clients to specific calculators (e.g., Small Producer Relief, Capital Allowances, Self‑Assessment, VAT) to improve accuracy
Record tool usage and outcomes for client records and future reference

items.title: HMRC Trusts and Estates newsletters
items.description: Newsletters published by HMRC, giving updates and guidance on Inheritance Tax and trusts.
items.changeNote: The HMRC Trusts and Estates Newsletter for August 2026 has been added.

ai.summary: HMRC newsletters provide trusts and estates practitioners with the latest non‑binding news and views as of their publication date, with older issues available via the National Archives.
ai.whoAffected: trusts and estates practitioners (including advisers to SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and the self‑employed)
actions: Subscribe to the HMRC Trusts and Estates newsletters
Review each issue for updates relevant to client trusts or estates
Remember the content is not legally binding and confirm against current legislation
Access older newsletters through the National Archives when needed

items.title: Check your tax filing and payment deadlines
items.description: Use this tool to find out your tax deadlines and add them to your calendar.

ai.summary: The HMRC tool lets contractors, employers, self‑assessment and VAT users enter their details to get personalised tax filing and payment deadlines, which can be printed or added to digital calendars.
ai.whoAffected: Contractors (CIS), employers (PAYE), self‑assessment taxpayers and VAT‑registered businesses, including SMEs and the self‑employed
actions: Collect each client’s accounting period dates, tax payment method and filing method (online or post)
Enter the information into the HMRC deadline tool to generate specific dates
Print the deadline list or add it to the client’s calendar (use Safari for Apple Calendar on iPhone/iPad)
Remind clients to file returns and pay taxes by the generated deadlines

items.title: Consultation on Simplifying Treaty Relief from Withholding Tax on Interest Paid Overseas
items.description: We welcome views on simplification of the process to obtain treaty relief in relation to withholding tax obligations when making payments of interest overseas.
items.changeNote: Updated to include information for a virtual roundtable event.

ai.summary: HMRC is consulting on simplifying the process for obtaining treaty relief from withholding tax on overseas interest payments, aiming to ease administration while preventing avoidance. Stakeholders are invited to a virtual roundtable on 3 Sept 2026 and to submit written views.
ai.whoAffected: Taxpayers making interest payments overseas, especially those involved in cross‑border financing and using existing treaty relief processes (e.g., Double Taxation Treaty Passport, Directions to make payments at the treaty rate).
actions: Identify clients who make overseas interest payments and may need treaty relief
Review their current treaty relief processes (Double Taxation Treaty Passport, Directions, claims)
Register for the virtual roundtable by emailing the address before 26 Aug 2026 (max 2 participants per firm)
Prepare and submit written responses to the consultation
legislationRefs: Directions to make payments at the treaty rate

items.title: Changes and issues affecting the Corporation Tax online service
items.description: Check changes and issues that may affect how you file your Company Tax Return.
items.changeNote: ‘First-year allowances for zero-emission cars and electric vehicle charge points’ section has been updated to include electric vehicle charge points. ‘New requirements for Corporation Tax computation format’ section has been updated with the work HMRC are doing to standardise the format for computations.

ai.summary: HMRC will add new CT600 boxes for a 40% first‑year allowance (from 1 Jan 2026) and extend 100% FYA for zero‑emission cars and EV charge points to 31 Mar 2027. Updates to the online service and validation fixes for RDEC, creative‑industry reliefs and loans to participators are due in April 2027, with a new computation format under development.
ai.whoAffected: All companies filing Corporation Tax returns, especially SMEs and owner‑managed businesses that claim capital allowances, R&D credits, creative‑industry reliefs, or have loans to participators
ai.effectiveDate: 1 Jan 2026 (40% FYA); 31 Mar 2027 (100% FYA extension); 6 Apr 2026 (loan rate); April 2027 (online service updates)
actions: Add the new CT600 boxes (725, 750, 760) to client filing templates for the 40% first‑year allowance
Guide clients to use the correct boxes for zero‑emission car and EV charge point allowances based on their accounting period
Check RDEC exemption claims so box L75 equals L70 and note the validation issue until April 2027
Include CT600P for creative‑industry reliefs and apply the £1 workaround for cultural relief validation errors
legislationRefs: section CTA09/S1112E of the Corporation Tax Act (CTA) 2009

items.title: HMRC email updates, videos and webinars for company directors
items.description: Learn more about your responsibilities as a company director.
items.changeNote: The live webinar link for ‘Company directors — payroll and you’ has been updated. The recorded webinar link for ‘The Informants Scheme — reporting tax fraud or avoidance’ has been added.

ai.summary: HMRC offers email updates, webinars and videos covering Self Assessment, Corporation Tax, payroll for directors, work‑from‑home expenses and R&D relief, helping company directors understand responsibilities, record‑keeping and claim processes.
ai.whoAffected: Company directors, particularly those of SMEs and self‑employed owners, as well as their tax agents
actions: Subscribe clients to the HMRC help and support email service to receive updates
Register directors for the live “payroll and you” webinar and review the recorded sessions
Advise clients to watch videos on work‑related and home‑working expenses to ensure correct claims
Guide clients on adding taxes (Corporation Tax, PAYE, VAT) via their business tax account

items.title: CIC Accounts User Feedback
items.description: Companies House want to hear your experiences of using the Package Accounts Upload Service

ai.summary: Companies House invites directors of Community Interest Companies who filed accounts online via the Package Accounts Upload Service to give feedback through a survey, aiming to improve filing services.
ai.whoAffected: Directors of Community Interest Companies that have used the Package Accounts Upload Service to file their CIC accounts online
actions: Identify CIC clients who used the Package Accounts Upload Service
Encourage those directors to complete the feedback survey via the provided link
Record any feedback received for internal reference
Monitor future Companies House updates for service changes

items.title: Apply to protect your details on the Companies House register
items.description: For company directors, LLP members or people with significant control (PSCs) who are at serious risk and want to protect their personal information from the public.
items.changeNote:
Online service to apply to protect your details has been withdrawn while we develop new services. Users can continue to apply using the paper form.

Also edited section "If your application is refused". If your application is refused we will refund your application fee.

ai.summary: Directors, LLP members and PSCs at serious risk can apply by paper to protect home address or all personal details from public view; protection hides data from credit agencies and is granted after review, costing £100 (or £15 for abbreviated).
ai.whoAffected: Company directors, LLP members and persons with significant control (PSCs) of SMEs or owner‑managed businesses who face serious risk of violence or intimidation.
actions: Identify clients at risk and advise them of the protection option
Collect supporting evidence and complete the appropriate paper form
Submit the application with the correct fee by post to Companies House
Notify clients of the decision, update any changes and advise on appeal or refund if refused

items.title: Fit and proper criteria for Authorised Corporate Service Providers
items.description: How the registrar will assess whether an applicant, or existing Authorised Corporate Service Provider (ACSP), is fit and proper to carry out the functions of an ACSP.

ai.summary: The registrar must refuse or can suspend an Authorised Corporate Service Provider (ACSP) if they are not fit and proper, assessing eligibility, AML supervision, criminal/regulatory history, honesty and compliance, with ongoing monitoring after registration.
ai.whoAffected: Applicants for ACSP registration and existing Authorised Corporate Service Providers, including any connected entities such as limited companies.
actions: Ensure clients provide accurate, complete information on ACSP applications
Review clients' AML supervisory status and any past suspensions or cessations
Check for criminal convictions, bankruptcies, director disqualifications or regulatory findings
Advise clients to promptly report any changes and cooperate with Companies House enquiries

items.title: Double Taxation Treaty Passport Scheme register
items.description: Check the status of overseas corporate lenders who are passport holders for Double Taxation Relief on UK loan interest.
items.changeNote: The register has been updated with 446 additions, 28 amendments and 219 removals.

ai.summary: The register lists companies in the Double Taxation Treaty Passport Scheme and lets borrowers verify a lender’s passport holder status; HMRC updates it regularly.
ai.whoAffected: Borrowers (including SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and the self‑employed) seeking UK loan interest relief
actions: Access the Double Taxation Treaty Passport Scheme register on the GOV.UK site
Check the lender’s name against the register to confirm passport holder status
Advise clients to rely on the register verification before finalising loan arrangements
Monitor the register periodically as HMRC adds new lenders

items.title: Directors disqualified for a total of 70 years following Companies House prosecutions
items.description: Twenty three company directors were disqualified in the first 6 months of this year for persistent or serious non-compliance with their responsibilities.

ai.summary: Companies House prosecuted 23 directors in early 2026 for persistent non‑filing, issuing disqualifications totalling 70 years and fines. Late filing triggers automatic penalties for companies and can lead to criminal prosecution of directors under the Companies Act 2006.
ai.whoAffected: Company directors and the companies they run, especially SMEs and owner‑managed businesses
actions: Ensure annual accounts and confirmation statements are filed by the statutory deadline
Set up a compliance calendar and monitoring system for each client
Advise directors of the personal risk of prosecution and disqualification for late filing
Review Companies House guidance and enforcement policy with clients

items.title: Who should register for VAT (VAT Notice 700/1)
items.description: Find out when and how to register for VAT.
items.changeNote: VAT Notice 700/1: supplement been updated with the thresholds for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027

ai.summary: VAT registration is required for anyone making business supplies of goods or services in the UK, importing goods, handling import acquisitions in Northern Ireland, or selling certain assets.
ai.whoAffected: UK‑based businesses of any size, including SMEs, owner‑managed firms and the self‑employed, that supply goods/services, import goods or acquisitions, or sell specified assets
actions: Identify clients who make UK business supplies, import goods, handle NI import acquisitions or sell certain assets
Check whether their turnover exceeds the updated registration thresholds for 1 April 2026‑31 March 2027
Advise qualifying clients to register for VAT promptly
Assist clients with completing and submitting the VAT registration form

items.title: Employment related securities bulletin 68 (August 2026)
items.description: Read about changes to employment related securities (ERS) net settlement reporting requirements, Save As You Earn (SAYE) guidance and Enterprise Management Incentives (EMI).

ai.summary: Employers must now report ERS net settlement with one row per employee, keep records for the tax year plus six years, and follow updated SAYE prospectus rules. EMI notification is removed from 6 April 2027, with grants reported via the EMI end‑of‑year return from the 2027‑28 tax year.
ai.whoAffected: Employers of SMEs and owner‑managed businesses using employment‑related securities, SAYE schemes, or Enterprise Management Incentives (EMI).
ai.effectiveDate: 6 April 2027 (EMI notification removal; ERS change applies to all tax years)
actions: Update client ERS end‑of‑year returns to use a single row per employee and omit the two previous lines
Ensure clients retain Income Tax and NI records for the current tax year plus six years and can produce them on request
Check SAYE schemes comply with Schedule 3 of the Income Tax (Earnings and Pensions) Act 2003 and paragraph 21 of the prospectus, especially the ban on transferring contracts
Advise EMI clients that from 6 April 2027 no notification is needed and that grants must be reported via the EMI end‑of‑year return starting the 2027‑28 tax year (submission from 6 April 2028)
legislationRefs: Schedule 3 of the Income Tax (Earnings and Pensions) Act 2003

items.title: How to complete an Other Interest return
items.description: How to complete and submit an Other Interest (OI) return using the HMRC spreadsheet or electronic flat text file.
items.changeNote: Information about submitting your return securely to HMRC has been updated in the section 'Submitting your return'.

ai.summary: HMRC may require an Other Interest return when you pay or receive interest for UK‑resident individuals. Returns must use the HMRC spreadsheet or approved flat file, be correctly labelled, and submitted by the due date, with penalties for errors or late filing.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses or organisations that pay interest to, or receive interest on behalf of, a reportable individual (UK‑resident), including SMEs, owner‑managed firms and the self‑employed.
actions: Check if the client pays interest to or receives interest for a UK‑resident individual and therefore needs an OI return
Choose the approved format (HMRC spreadsheet or electronic flat text file) and ensure each file is labelled with HMRC reference, sub‑return number, batch number, total batches and year
Complete the spreadsheet following the mandatory field rules and use the built‑in error validation to correct any issues before submission
Submit the return by the statutory due date, email HMRC by 31 January for sub‑return number changes and label all files correctly; avoid zipping files

items.title: How to complete your statutory notice return
items.description: How to download and complete your spreadsheet return templates and send them to HMRC.
items.changeNote: Information about submitting your return online has been updated.

ai.summary: If you receive a statutory notice under Schedule 23 Finance Act 2011 or Section 887 Income Tax Act 2007, you must download the correct spreadsheet template, complete only the required fields without altering its structure, name it as instructed, and submit it to HMRC by the deadline via the secure service or email.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses or individuals (including SMEs, owner‑managed firms and the self‑employed) that have been issued a statutory notice under Schedule 23 of the Finance Act 2011 or under Section 887 of the Income Tax Act 2007
actions: Download the appropriate template from GOV.UK using the filename in the notice
Complete only the required fields, keep the original sheet layout and include correct currency codes
Name the file following the notice’s naming convention and submit by the deadline via the Secure Data Exchange Service or email (splitting files >8 MB)
If the return exceeds 65,000 rows or you need assistance, contact Statutory notice information returns enquiries
legislationRefs: Section 887 of the Income Tax Act 2007

items.title: How to complete a bank and building society interest return
items.description: Find out how to complete and submit a return using the HMRC spreadsheet or electronic flat text file (EFTF).
items.changeNote: Information about transferring files securely with HMRC has been updated in the section 'Submitting your return'.

ai.summary: HMRC requires banks and building societies to submit annual interest returns via a specific spreadsheet or flat file, correctly labelled and formatted, with sub‑return numbers reported by 31 January. Errors can cause penalties, so use the official spreadsheet, validate data, and follow labelling rules.
ai.whoAffected: UK banks and building societies (and their reporting teams) that must file Bank and Building Society Interest returns
actions: Use the latest HMRC spreadsheet or approved flat file format; do not reformat or zip files
Label each file with HMRC reference, sub‑return number, batch number, total batches and year as specified
Notify HMRC by 31 January of any new or discontinued sub‑return numbers via the provided email address
Check the spreadsheet’s error validation, correct all highlighted errors before submission and avoid resubmitting full returns for omissions

items.title: Disclosure of tax avoidance schemes: guidance
items.description: This guidance will help you work out if you need to tell HMRC that you use or promote a tax avoidance scheme.
items.changeNote: The mailing address in 'section 1.5 Help and advice' has been updated.

ai.summary: If a business or individual promotes or uses a scheme that gives a tax or National Insurance advantage, they may have to disclose it to HMRC.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses, owners, advisers or self‑employed persons who promote or use arrangements designed to obtain a tax or NI advantage
actions: Check client activities for any promotion or use of tax advantage schemes
Assess whether the activity triggers a disclosure requirement under the guidance
Prepare the required tax avoidance scheme disclosure for HMRC
Submit the disclosure and retain supporting documentation

items.title: Chancellor letter to the Treasury Select Committee (TSC) - Budget 2026 date
items.description: The Chancellor has today written to the Treasury Select Committee (TSC) to confirm the date of the budget.

ai.summary: The Budget is scheduled for 28 October 2026.
ai.whoAffected: Not stated in source
actions: Add the budget date to client planning calendars
Notify clients of the upcoming budget date
Prepare to review any tax changes announced on that date
Schedule a post‑budget briefing for clients

items.title: Budget to move “power and money out of Westminster, and into every postcode around Britain”.
items.description: Today (Friday 31 July), the Chancellor has confirmed that the date of the Budget will be Wednesday 28 October.

ai.summary: The Chancellor announced the first Budget will be on Wednesday 28 October, promising to shift money and power from Westminster to every postcode, built on fiscal discipline and aimed at giving businesses and families stability.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses and families across the UK
actions: Watch the Chancellor’s announcement video
Submit comments via the Budget Representation Portal before 23:59 on Wednesday 9 September
Inform clients of the upcoming Budget on 28 October
Prepare to discuss potential fiscal measures and stability for business planning

items.title: When you need to verify your identity for Companies House
items.description: When you need to verify depends on your role, and when you started that role.
items.changeNote: Added text to explain you do not need to complete identity verification for a PSC who has died. The PSC should remain on the Companies House register until a grant of probate or letters of administration have been received.

ai.summary: Directors must give their Companies House personal code on each confirmation statement or new registration; PSCs need to verify identity within specific 14‑day periods, with special rules for deceased PSCs; authorised corporate service providers must verify identity to act as agents; other roles will face verification later.
ai.whoAffected: Company directors, people with significant control (PSCs), authorised corporate service providers, and future roles such as filing persons, limited partnerships, corporate directors and members, and corporate PSC officers
actions: Check each client director’s need to supply a personal code on confirmation statements and new company filings
Confirm PSCs submit their personal code within the correct 14‑day window, noting the exemption for deceased PSCs
Verify that any ACSP client has completed identity verification before registering as a Companies House authorised agent
Track upcoming identity‑verification requirements for other roles to advise clients when they become applicable

items.title: People with significant control (PSCs)
items.description: How to identify and record the people who own or control your company.
items.changeNote: Added text to explain you do not need to complete identity verification for a PSC who has died. The PSC should remain on the Companies House register until a grant of probate or letters of administration have been received.

ai.summary: Companies must identify any person with significant control (PSC), record their details, and submit them to Companies House, including identity verification within 14 days (except deceased PSCs until probate). Changes must be reported within 14 days, and a PSC statement is required if no PSC exists.
ai.whoAffected: Limited companies, including SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and self‑employed individuals operating through a company
actions: Identify any individuals meeting PSC criteria using the register of members and company constitution
Collect required PSC details and obtain their confirmation, including name, DOB, nationality, addresses, dates and nature of control
Submit the PSC information to Companies House and ensure the PSC provides their personal code within the 14‑day verification period (exempt deceased PSCs until probate)
Notify Companies House of any PSC detail changes within 14 days or file a PSC statement if the company has no PSC

items.title: Employment intermediaries reporting requirements
items.description: Find guidance about the reports that intermediaries need to send to HMRC where they do not operate Pay As You Earn.
items.changeNote: Guidance on 'How to sign in' has been updated in the ‘What this means for an agent' attachment.

ai.summary: Employment intermediaries that place workers and do not operate PAYE must report all placed workers to HMRC using the prescribed template, uploading via the online service at least every three months, unless they are UK employers who operate PAYE for supplied workers.
ai.whoAffected: Employment intermediaries (agencies) that place workers for clients and do not run PAYE, and UK employers who supply workers and operate PAYE (exempt).
actions: Identify whether the client is an intermediary without PAYE or a UK employer operating PAYE
If an intermediary, create reports using HMRC’s report template
Upload and send the reports via HMRC’s online service at least quarterly (or more frequently as chosen)
Confirm exemption criteria are met for UK employers operating PAYE to avoid reporting

items.title: Get help with a tax issue as a public body
items.description: Get help with a tax issue if you're a public body by reading guidance and manuals, or filling in the public body queries form.
items.changeNote: Information has been added to the 'Who can get help' section to clarify who can get support from HMRC's Public Bodies Group. The 'Before you start' section has been added to give information on what to do before contacting HMRC and when to use the public body queries form. The 'Fill in the public body queries form' section has been added to give more information on how to fill in the form.

ai.summary: Public bodies can get HMRC help for tax issues by first reading guidance, then using the public body queries form to raise processing or technical issues or request non‑statutory clearance, providing required details and tax references.
ai.whoAffected: Public bodies such as NHS, government departments, police, fire and rescue services, housing associations, local authorities, higher and further education institutions, political parties, trade unions, trade or membership associations, worshipful companies and guilds.
actions: Confirm the client qualifies as a public body under the listed categories.
Read the relevant HMRC guidance and manuals before contacting HMRC.
Gather all required information: query details, proposed resolution, supporting evidence and the organisation’s tax reference.
Complete the online public body queries form and send it to HMRC by the email or postal address provided.

items.title: IFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements Exposure Draft
items.description: Public consultation on HM Treasury proposals for the application of IFRS 18 Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements across Central Government

ai.summary: HM Treasury is consulting on applying the new IFRS 18 standard across Central Government and seeks comments on its proposed approach.
ai.whoAffected: Central Government bodies
actions: Review the IFRS 18 consultation document
Submit comments if your practice or clients are interested
Monitor updates on any future implementation decisions
Inform relevant clients about the potential impact of the new standard

items.title: HMRC urges customers not to ignore Simple Assessment letters
items.description: HMRC is urging customers who receive a Simple Assessment letter this summer to check it carefully and pay any tax owed by the deadline.

ai.summary: HMRC will send Simple Assessment (PA302) letters this summer for the 2025‑26 tax year to anyone with untaxed income. Recipients must check the details and pay any tax due by 31 January 2027 (or the date shown) using the HMRC app or other methods.
ai.whoAffected: Individuals and businesses with tax owed on interest, dividends, a second income, pension income, excess tax‑free allowance or larger untaxed amounts that cannot be collected through PAYE or Self Assessment.
ai.effectiveDate: 31 January 2027 (unless a different date is shown)
actions: Ask clients to review any Simple Assessment letter as soon as it arrives
Compare the tax figures in the letter with the client’s own records
Arrange payment – in full or instalments – via the HMRC app, online, bank transfer or cheque before the deadline
Direct clients to GOV.UK for guidance, authenticity checks and support resources

items.title: UK pension giants join forces to unlock £1bn to back Britain’s innovators
items.description: Pension fund could be used to back the next generation of high-growth British science and technology companies.

ai.summary: Major UK pension providers plan a £1 billion Scale‑up Fund to invest in high‑growth British science and technology companies, aiming to give pension savers returns while providing growth capital for innovators and creating skilled jobs.
ai.whoAffected: Pension savers/members and UK high‑growth businesses, including SMEs and scale‑ups seeking capital
actions: Track the progress of the proposed UK Scale‑up Fund and its launch timeline
Advise client businesses on preparing investment‑ready documentation to attract pension‑capital funding
Inform pension‑savvy clients about the potential new avenue for long‑term returns
Encourage interested asset managers to contact the British Business Bank as indicated

items.title: Public service pensions remedy newsletter — July 2026
items.description: This newsletter is published by HMRC’s Pension Schemes Services to update stakeholders on the latest news on the public service pensions remedy.

ai.summary: The July 2026 newsletter outlines updates on the public service pensions remedy, including new regulations, election deadlines, calculation service, immediate detriment, armed forces scheme elections, tax treatment of trivial commutation lump sum death benefits, reporting deadlines after death, excess teacher service and a transitional tax‑free amount certificate.

Prepare the SH19 form plus the resolution, solvency statement and directors' statement as required
If no court order, upload supporting documents first then the SH19 online; if a court order, post all documents to Companies House
Select standard or same‑day service, note the applicable fee and processing time
legislationRefs: section 644 and 649 of the Companies Act 2006

items.title: Change a company name (NM01)
items.description: Use this form to give notice of an unconditional change of name by resolution.
items.changeNote: Removed message about delays to filings, as our filings are now being processed as normal.

ai.summary: Changing a company’s registered name requires a special resolution and filing a form; paper filings cost £30, online filings cost £20 (or £85 for same‑day service).
ai.whoAffected: Companies, including SMEs and owner‑managed businesses, that wish to change their registered name
actions: Prepare a special resolution to change the company name
Choose filing method: paper form (£30) or online service (£20 or £85 for same‑day)
Make the cheque payable to ‘Companies House’ if using paper
Submit the form and pay the fee to Companies House

items.title: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Supervision Reform: Duties, Powers, and Accountability Consultation
items.description: This consultation covers subsidiary considerations related to the FCA taking over professional services firms' anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing supervision.

ai.summary: The government proposes that the FCA take over AML/CTF supervision of legal, accountancy, and trust and company service providers, outlining new duties, powers and accountability, with a consultation running 6 Nov‑24 Dec 2025.
ai.whoAffected: Legal firms, accountancy firms and trust/company service providers (and their SME, owner‑managed and self‑employed clients)
actions: Monitor the consultation period (6 Nov‑24 Dec 2025)
Review current AML/CTF procedures in anticipation of FCA oversight
Align policies with the proposed FCA duties, powers and accountability mechanisms
Submit feedback to anti‑moneylaunderingbranch@hmtreasury.gov.uk before the deadline

items.title: Great British Summer Savings: Major businesses pass on VAT cut to families on days out
items.description: Some of the UK’s most prominent leisure and hospitality businesses have committed to passing on summer savings to families as they met the Chancellor today – ahead of the government’s Great British Summer Savings scheme going live.

ai.summary: Major leisure businesses will pass on the temporary VAT cut under the Great British Summer Savings scheme, reducing costs of children’s meals, tickets and attractions from 25 June, with all families eligible and free bus travel for children 5‑15 in August.
ai.whoAffected: Families with children (including those aged 5‑15) and leisure/hospitality SMEs such as cinemas, theme parks, pubs and restaurants offering eligible meals and tickets
actions: Ensure client pricing reflects the temporary VAT cut on eligible children’s meals and tickets
Download and use the government digital toolkit for promotional stickers, posters and materials
Inform customers about free local bus travel for children aged five to fifteen throughout August
Track footfall and revenue changes to demonstrate the scheme’s benefit

items.title: UK issues largest penalty for financial sanctions breaches since Russia’s 2022 illegal invasion of Ukraine
items.description: The United Kingdom has imposed its largest ever penalty for a breach of Russian financial sanctions since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine.

ai.summary: The UK’s OFSI fined travel tech firm Sabre Global Technologies over £1 million for repeatedly breaching Russia sanctions, including circumvention by routing payments through a non‑UK account, highlighting the need for robust senior oversight and sanctions risk management.
ai.whoAffected: UK businesses, including SMEs and self‑employed firms, that provide services or payments to parties that could be designated under the Russia sanctions regime.
actions: Review and update client sanctions screening procedures regularly
Establish clear senior oversight of sanctions compliance within the firm
Implement controls to prevent circumvention, such as monitoring alternative payment routes
Encourage voluntary disclosure and cooperate fully with OFSI if a breach is identified

Monitor updates to the manual for any changes affecting public‑sector reporting
Inform SME clients that this guidance does not directly impact private‑sector reporting

items.title: Progress made in cleaning up Companies House register as further steps taken to tackle economic crime
items.description: A new report released today reveals the strides being made to improve the accuracy of the Companies House register and disrupt economic crime.

ai.summary: The Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 reforms have introduced mandatory identity verification, removed fraudulent addresses and boosted enforcement, improving Companies House data accuracy and protecting businesses from fraud.
ai.whoAffected: SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and self‑employed who rely on Companies House information for credit, purchasing and compliance decisions
actions: Ensure client directors and secretaries have completed identity verification and linked appointments
Check and update client company addresses on the register to remove outdated or fraudulent entries
Monitor the Companies House register for suspicious entries affecting clients and advise corrective action
Incorporate the new offences under the ECCT Act into client risk assessments and compliance advice

section 213(1) of the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023

ai.whoAffected: Office for Budget Responsibility and its Board members
actions: Note the change in OBR non‑executive membership for future commentary
Monitor OBR publications for any shifts in fiscal outlook
Inform clients that the leadership change does not affect current tax rules
Stay alert for any new OBR guidance that may arise from the new appointment

items.title: Searching the Companies House register
items.description: Using our Find and update company information service to follow companies and search company information for free.
items.changeNote: 'Service information' section updated - 'Links to external websites'. Information added about content including 2D optical codes.

ai.summary: Companies House’s Find and update service provides free access to company data, including basic details, filings, officers and dissolved records, and offers a free ‘Follow’ email alert. Records of dissolved companies will now be kept for up to 20 years.

actions: Use the free Find and update service to obtain client company details for due‑diligence checks
Register and use the ‘Follow’ feature to receive email alerts on client or competitor filings
Advise clients to review officer information as dissolved records will be retained longer
If required, access real‑time data via the Companies House API while respecting acceptable‑use limits
legislationRefs: Corporate Transparency and Register Reform consultation
The Reports on Payments to Governments Regulations 2014

items.title: Insolvency Service continues crackdown on companies exploiting UK business register for China-based clients
items.description: Five companies shut down this year following Insolvency Service investigations

ai.summary: The Insolvency Service has wound up two firms that registered over 4,300 UK companies for mainly China‑based clients, breaching AML rules and operating without HMRC approval, highlighting abuse of Companies House and the need for accurate, transparent company information.
ai.whoAffected: UK businesses that use third‑party registered office or company secretarial services, directors, and firms acting as trust or company service providers
actions: Confirm any service provider acting as a trust or company service provider is registered with HMRC
Carry out AML and identity checks on any third‑party address or secretarial service before recommending it
Advise clients to ensure all Companies House information is accurate and to avoid unregistered brokers
Monitor Companies House filings for signs of abuse and report concerns to the Insolvency Service
legislationRefs: Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023

items.title: Companies House to bring in changes to accounts filing from April 2028
items.description: Small companies and micro-entities to file profit and loss accounts but can opt out of publication. All companies will need to file accounts via commercial software with more time to prepare.

ai.summary: From April 2028, all UK companies must file annual accounts in iXBRL using commercial software; small companies and micro‑entities must also file profit and loss statements but can opt out of public publication. Abridged accounts are removed, audit‑exemption statements are strengthened, and component parts must be filed together.
ai.whoAffected: All UK registered companies, including small companies, micro‑entities and those using accountants or third‑party agents
actions: Ensure clients prepare profit and loss accounts for filing and discuss the opt‑out option for small companies and micro‑entities
Select and implement an approved commercial iXBRL software solution for filing accounts
Update internal filing procedures to submit full accounts together and discontinue abridged accounts
Communicate the new requirements and timelines to clients and adjust engagement letters accordingly
legislationRefs: Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023

Ensure small‑company and micro‑entity clients prepare profit‑and‑loss accounts
Advise eligible clients on opting out of publication
Update internal filing timelines to use the extended preparation period
legislationRefs: Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023

items.description: Small businesses struggling with finances to receive £4 million funding boost to business debt advice services through the Money and Pensions Service.

actions: Alert clients that enhanced Business Debtline support is available

items.title: Verifying your identity for Companies House
items.description: You need to prove who you are to set up, run, own or control a company in the UK.
items.changeNote: In the 'Who needs to verify' section, removed 'someone who files for a company - for example, a company secretary' .

ai.summary: Identity verification is now a legal requirement for directors, equivalent officers, overseas directors, persons with significant control and authorised corporate service providers. Verification is done once via GOV.UK One Login or an ACSP, producing a personal code that must be used in filings. Non‑compliance can lead to offences and penalties.
ai.whoAffected: Directors, members, general partners, managing officers, overseas company directors, persons with significant control (PSCs), and Authorised Corporate Service Providers (ACSPs). Future groups include people who file at Companies House, limited partnerships, corporate directors, corporate LLP members and corporate PSC officers.
actions: Identify which of your clients fall into the director, PSC or ACSP categories and need to verify their identity
Advise clients to verify using the GOV.UK One Login service or an authorised corporate service provider, providing required documents
Ensure clients obtain their Companies House personal code and include it in confirmation statements, director appointments and PSC filings
Monitor verification deadlines and warn clients of the offences and penalties for non‑compliance

items.title: Using an Authorised Corporate Service Provider (ACSP) to verify your identity
items.description: How to find an ACSP, what an ACSP needs to verify your identity for Companies House, and what happens after an ACSP verifies your identity.

ai.summary: To verify a client’s identity for Companies House you can act as an Authorised Corporate Service Provider (ACSP). Provide the client’s name, address, email and approved ID evidence, then receive a personal code by email which links the verification to the public register.
ai.whoAffected: Individuals who need to verify their identity for Companies House – e.g., directors, shareholders or anyone filing through an accountant or solicitor.
actions: Confirm your firm is registered with Companies House as an ACSP and is AML‑supervised
Collect the client’s full name, home address, email and acceptable identity evidence as advised by Companies House
Submit the verification to Companies House and ensure the client’s email is correct to receive the personal code
Advise the client to check for the email (including spam), update their email address if it changes, and explain the verification statement that will appear on the public register

items.title: Registrar's rules
items.description: Rules outlining the form, manner of delivery and method of authentication for documents delivered to Companies House in electronic or paper format.
items.changeNote: Updated Registrar’s Rules – Volume 8: Identity Verification by the Registrar. Updated required evidence to allow UK driving licences expired within 90 days, removed health and education records, and excluded replaced passports

ai.summary: The Registrar’s Rules – Volume 8 was amended on 20 May 2026 (effective 22 May 2026) to accept UK driving licences expired within 90 days as identity evidence, remove health and education records, and exclude replaced passports. This changes the proof of identity required for Companies House filings.
ai.whoAffected: All companies, authorised corporate service providers and their clients—including SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and the self‑employed—who need to verify identity for filing documents with Companies House.
actions: Update client ID checklists to accept UK driving licences expired up to 90 days
Remove health and education records from required identity documents
Ensure replaced passports are no longer accepted as evidence
Notify staff and clients of the new evidence rules

items.title: Great British Summer Savings 2026: Family activities VAT relief fact sheet
items.description: From 25 June to 1 September 2026 the Government is introducing a temporary reduced rate of VAT on children's menu meals in restaurants and family leisure activities over the summer period, cutting VAT from 20% to 5%.

ai.summary: From 25 June to 1 September 2026 a temporary 5% VAT rate replaces the standard 20% on eligible children’s meals in restaurants and family tickets for cinemas, theatres, attractions and similar leisure activities across the UK, plus free bus travel for children 5‑15 in England during August.
ai.whoAffected: Families with children, especially those aged 5‑15; restaurants, cinemas, theatres, amusement parks, museums, zoos, soft‑play centres and other eligible leisure providers; and any business selling qualifying children’s meals or tickets.
ai.effectiveDate: 25 June 2026 – 1 September 2026 (VAT relief); August 2026 (free bus travel for children 5‑15 in England)
actions: Identify client businesses that sell eligible children’s meals or tickets and confirm the dates they fall within the relief period.
Advise them to apply the 5% VAT rate on qualifying sales and, where possible, reduce prices so the saving is passed to families at the till.
Ensure they record which sales are eligible and consider applying the reduced rate or issuing a VAT refund for sales made before the legislation took effect.
Direct clients to HMRC guidance for detailed rules and any sector‑specific queries.

items.title: Great British Summer Savings: VAT slashed to save families money on days out
items.description: Families will enjoy discounted attractions and meals out this summer, with the launch of the government’s Great British Summer Savings scheme to help people enjoy day out for less.

ai.summary: From 25 June to 1 September 2026 VAT on children’s meals, family tickets and many attractions falls from 20% to 5% across the UK, and children 5‑15 in England travel free on local buses in August, boosting footfall for hospitality and leisure firms.
ai.whoAffected: Families with children, restaurants, cinemas, theatres, amusement parks and other attractions, and any business selling eligible tickets or meals; also children aged 5‑15 in England using local bus services.
actions: Check client eligibility for the reduced 5% VAT rate on children’s meals and tickets and adjust VAT returns accordingly
Update pricing and invoicing systems to apply the 5% rate and retain evidence of eligible sales
Advise clients to communicate the VAT saving to customers and monitor that the benefit is passed on
Inform clients of the free‑bus travel for children 5‑15 in England during August and the 10p‑per‑mile increase in tax‑free mileage rates for 2026‑27

items.title: Companies House and Intellectual Property Office (IPO) join forces to warn about unsolicited payment requests
items.description: Companies House and IPO warn businesses about unsolicited payment requests and how to identify them.

ai.summary: Companies House and the IPO warn that scammers send fake invoices for their services; these may arrive by post or email, request inflated fees, and appear to be official. Verify addresses, check for non‑government disclaimers, contact the agencies before paying, and report any suspicious requests.
ai.whoAffected: All businesses, including SMEs, owner‑managed firms and the self‑employed, that may receive unsolicited payment requests claiming to be from Companies House or the IPO.
actions: Check website and email domains on any invoice; official services use GOV.UK addresses
Look for disclaimers stating the sender is not affiliated with government
Contact Companies House or the IPO directly to verify any payment request before paying
Report suspicious invoices to Report Fraud and the local Trading Standards office

items.title: FS Sector Strategy: Review of the Financial Ombudsman Service
items.description: A consultation on the government’s proposed reforms to the Financial Ombudsman Service (FOS), following the Economic Secretary’s review.
items.changeNote: paragraph 2.19 removed from consultation outcome document.

ai.summary: The government proposes reforms to the Financial Ombudsman Service’s legislative framework to stop it acting as a quasi‑regulator and to ensure it remains an impartial dispute‑resolution service, giving consumers and firms more certainty and predictability.
ai.whoAffected: Consumers and firms that use the Financial Ombudsman Service, including SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and the self‑employed
actions: Monitor the consultation and any forthcoming legislation
Inform clients of potential changes to FOS dispute handling
Review internal complaint procedures to align with anticipated reforms
Prepare guidance for clients on using the FOS under the new framework

items.title: Fairer taxes for high-value homes
items.description: The government has launched a consultation on the details of the new High Value Council Tax Surcharge, to make the system fairer for households.

ai.summary: The government is consulting on a new High Value Council Tax Surcharge for England homes worth £2 million or more, targeting the top 1% of properties, with the charge starting in April 2028 after five‑year revaluations.
ai.whoAffected: Owners of residential property in England valued at £2 million or above (approximately the top 1% of homes) and any taxpayers affected by the surcharge process.
actions: Monitor the eight‑week consultation and note any client‑specific concerns
Advise high‑value property owners on the upcoming surcharge and potential financial impact
Prepare clients for the five‑year revaluation cycle and possible valuation reviews
Assist clients with billing, deferral options and any appeals process

Advise public‑sector employer clients on potential impact on future contribution rates

Update client pension cost‑control planning in line with the reformed mechanism under the 2013 and 2022 Acts

items.description: What the company register is, what details you need to give to Companies House, and how the public can access this information.

items.description: Sets out the main requirements for incorporating a limited liability partnership (LLP) in the UK.

ai.summary: The guide explains how to set up a limited liability partnership, choose a compliant name, and change the LLP name later.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses and individuals planning to incorporate a limited liability partnership, including SMEs, owner‑managed firms and the self‑employed
actions: Explain the incorporation process and required documentation to clients
Check proposed LLP names against the listed controls and restrictions
Assist clients in filing the incorporation with Companies House
Support any future LLP name changes or updates

items.title: Life of a limited liability partnership
items.description: Rules and requirements for limited liability partnerships registered in the UK.

ai.summary: The guide tells LLP members, designated members and advisers what filings are required with Companies House to keep the LLP on the public register.
ai.whoAffected: Members or designated members of limited liability partnerships and advisers to LLPs (including SME and owner‑managed LLPs).
actions: Identify the specific Companies House filing requirements for each LLP client
Set up a filing calendar to ensure deadlines are met
Prepare and submit the required documents on behalf of the LLP
Maintain records to demonstrate ongoing compliance

items.title: Scottish qualifying partnerships: People with significant control
items.description: What information Scottish qualifying partnerships (SQPs) need to file at Companies House about people with significant control (PSCs).

ai.summary: The guide tells directors, secretaries and advisers of Scottish qualifying partnerships how to register as a qualifying partnership and what PSC information must be filed with Companies House.
ai.whoAffected: Directors, secretaries and advisers to Scottish qualifying partnerships
actions: Register the partnership as a qualifying partnership
Identify persons with significant control (PSCs)
Collect the required PSC information
Submit the PSC details to Companies House

items.title: Register a charge (mortgage) for a limited company
items.description: How to register a new charge at Companies House, or tell us about any you've paid off.

ai.summary: A charge (e.g., mortgage) must be registered with Companies House within 21 days of creation, using form MR01 online (fee £14) or paper (£24). Include a certified copy of the instrument, optionally redacting personal data. Registering later requires a court order. Keep records up‑to‑date and notify Companies House when a charge is satisfied or property released.
ai.whoAffected: Limited companies, limited liability partnerships, their lenders or agents, and any person interested in the charge
actions: Check that any new charge is registered within 21 days of creation
Obtain a certified copy of the charge instrument and redact allowed personal information
File the charge online using form MR01 (or paper form) and pay the £14 fee
Notify Companies House via MR04/MR05 when the charge is paid off or property is released

items.title: Register a limited partnership
items.description: How to register a limited partnership.

ai.summary: Guide for anyone registering, designating as a private fund, partnering in, or advising a limited partnership, including PSC rules for Scottish LPs.
ai.whoAffected: Individuals intending to register a limited partnership, private fund LPs, limited or general partners, and advisers to limited partnerships
actions: Confirm client’s role (registrant, private fund, partner or adviser)
Explain People with Significant Control rules for Scottish limited partnerships
Assist with the registration paperwork and filing requirements
Provide ongoing compliance advice for the partnership

items.title: UK Societas
items.description: Information on the administration and management of a UK Societas.

ai.summary: Guidance outlines that existing UK‑registered Societas Europaea were automatically turned into UK Societas from 1 Jan 2021. Affected entities can stay as a UK Societas, be wound up, or become a PLC; new SEs cannot be formed and UK branches must follow overseas company rules.
ai.whoAffected: Companies that were registered as Societas Europaea (SE) in the UK and UK branches of SEs registered in an EU member state
actions: Identify if the client is an SE still registered in the UK
Advise the client to remain a UK Societas, wind up, or convert to a PLC
Ensure any UK branch of an EU‑registered SE complies with overseas company regulations
Review the two EU Exit Regulations for compliance requirements
legislationRefs: The European Public Limited-Liability Company (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2018
The International Accounting Standards and European Public Limited-Liability Company (Amendment etc.) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019

items.title: UK economic interest groupings (UKEIG)
items.description: The main features of a UKEIG and what information you must register with Companies House.

ai.summary: Guidance outlines UKEIG features, who must register with Companies House, and notes that UK EEIGs were automatically converted on 1 Jan 2021. It applies to existing UKEIGs, prospective members/managers, and UK offices of overseas EEIGs.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses currently registered as EEIGs in the UK, members or managers of UKEIGs, and organisations establishing a UK office for an EEIG whose official address is outside the UK
actions: Confirm whether any client EEIG was registered in the UK before 1 Jan 2021 and note its automatic conversion to a UKEIG
Advise members and managers of UKEIGs on their Companies House filing obligations
Update client registration details with Companies House to reflect UKEIG status where required
Ensure clients setting up a UK office for a foreign EEIG comply with the UKEIG filing guidance
legislationRefs: The European Economic Interest Grouping (Amendment) (EU Exit) Regulations 2018

items.title: Confirmation statement for a Scottish limited partnership (SLP CS01)
items.description: Use this form to confirm that the Scottish limited partnership (SLP) details are up to date.

ai.summary: To file a Scottish limited partnership confirmation statement, complete and save the CS01 form, then upload it to Companies House online, paying the £110 fee by card. Online filing is faster than posting paper copies.
ai.whoAffected: Scottish limited partnerships that need to submit a confirmation statement (SLP CS01)
actions: Complete the SLP CS01 form
Save the completed form to your device
Upload the form to Companies House and pay the £110 fee by debit or credit card
Use the online filing service instead of posting to avoid longer processing times

items.title: Overseas companies: restricting disclosure of your address
items.description: How to restrict access to your address on the public register.

ai.summary: Guide for directors or permanent representatives of overseas companies with a UK establishment to apply to hide their residential address and suppress specified addresses on the public register.
ai.whoAffected: Directors or permanent representatives of overseas companies with a registered UK establishment, and advisers to such companies
actions: Identify clients who are directors or permanent representatives of overseas companies with a UK establishment
Prepare and submit the application to restrict disclosure of their residential address
Ensure any specified addresses are suppressed from the public register
Advise clients on ongoing compliance and record‑keeping requirements

items.title: Confirmation statement (CS01c)
items.description: You can use this form if your registered office address is situated in Wales (instead of England and Wales), to confirm that the company details are up to date.

ai.summary: The CS01c form lets Welsh‑registered companies confirm their details with Companies House, costing £110 on paper, with online filing available. It covers updates to SIC codes, capital, share trading status, PSC exemption, shareholders, and requires a registered email and director identity verification.
ai.whoAffected: Companies that have their registered office address in Wales and need to file a confirmation statement
actions: Check if any changes are needed to SIC codes, capital, share trading status, PSC exemption or shareholder details and complete parts 1‑4 accordingly
Ensure a registered email address is provided using part 5 if not already on record
Collect and submit identity verification details for all current directors
Advise filing the confirmation statement online to avoid the £110 paper fee

items.title: Confirmation statement for a limited liability partnership (LL CS01)
items.description: Use this form to confirm that your LLP's details are up to date.

ai.summary: The LL CS01 form confirms an LLP’s details on the Companies House register, requires a £110 paper filing fee, a registered email address, identity verification for all members, and special date rules when restoring a struck‑off LLP.
ai.whoAffected: Limited liability partnerships that need to file a confirmation statement
actions: Provide a registered email address in part 1 if not already on record
Submit identity verification details for all current members unless already provided
If restoring a struck‑off LLP, use the statement date that was due before strike‑off and contact Companies House if unsure
Pay the £110 fee when filing the statement on paper

items.title: Strike off a company from the register (DS01)
items.description: Use this service to apply to strike off a company from the Companies House register.

ai.summary: Apply to strike off a company using form DS01, ensuring all business closure duties are met; online applications cost £13, paper forms £18, and the company’s bank account freezes at dissolution with any assets passing to the Crown.
ai.whoAffected: Directors and owners of limited companies seeking to dissolve their business
actions: Confirm the client has fulfilled all closure responsibilities before filing
Choose online DS01 unless a paper form is required
Pay the correct fee (£13 online or £18 by cheque/postal order)
Warn that the bank account will be frozen and assets will pass to the Crown unless the company is restored

items.title: Filing your Companies House information online
items.description: How to send your information to Companies House using our online services.

ai.summary: From 13 Oct 2025 Companies House WebFiling will require a GOV.UK One Login, replacing the current sign‑in method. Companies must update email details, create or link a One Login, and ensure authorised company lists are current. Online filing saves time, money and reduces penalties, with built‑in checks and faster processing.
ai.whoAffected: All limited companies using Companies House WebFiling, including SMEs, owner‑managed businesses and self‑employed directors who file accounts, confirmation statements or other company information online.
actions: Update the email address on the client’s WebFiling account and match it to any Companies House account
Create a GOV.UK One Login for the client (using the same email) before 13 Oct 2025
Connect the client’s WebFiling account to GOV.UK One Login when signing in after 13 Oct 2025
Review the ‘Your companies’ list in WebFiling and remove any companies the client no longer files for

items.title: Apply for administrative restoration to the register (RT01)
items.description: Use this form to apply to restore a company to the Companies House register.

ai.summary: Apply for administrative restoration by submitting RT01 with required documents and fees (£341 plus £64 waiver) if the client was a director/shareholder of a trading company dissolved within 6 years; missing info or fee leads to rejection.
ai.whoAffected: Directors or shareholders of a company that was struck off and dissolved by the Registrar within the last 6 years while it was trading
actions: Confirm client meets eligibility (director/shareholder, dissolved within 6 years and was trading)
Collect completed RT01, any outstanding accounts or confirmation statements, late filing penalties and a bona vacantia waiver letter
Include the correct fees (£341 application fee and £64 waiver fee) with the submission
Post the full package to Companies House main office; advise client not to call for assistance

items.title: Sign in to your authorised agent account
items.description: You must be registered as an Authorised Corporate Service Provider (ACSP, also known as an authorised agent), or a user for an ACSP.

ai.summary: ACSPs and their users must sign in with GOV.UK One Login to access services like identity verification, view user lists, and manage account details; owners can update details within 14 days and close the account, while admins can manage users.
ai.whoAffected: Account owners, administrators and standard users of an Authorised Corporate Service Provider (ACSP), and the ACSP itself
actions: Ensure the client has a GOV.UK One Login to sign in to their authorised agent account
Advise owners to review and update ACSP details within 14 days of any change
Guide administrators on adding/removing users and assigning appropriate roles
Remind all users they can verify identities for Companies House and view the user list

items.title: The Local Government Finance Act 1988 (Calculation of Non-Domestic Rating Multipliers for Retail, Hospitality or Leisure) (England) Regulations 2026
items.description: Paragraphs A6A and 9B of Schedule 7 to the Local Government Finance Act 1988 (c. 41) (“the Act”) were inserted by the Non-Domestic Rating (Multipliers and Private Schools) Act 2025 (c. 12), enabling the Treasury to make regulations for additional non-domestic rating multipliers for the purpose of the calculation of business rates under the Act. These Regulations specify the additional multipliers

items.title: Register of Overseas Entities: approach to enforcement
items.description: This framework explains how Companies House will use its enforcement powers in relation to the Register of Overseas Entities.
items.changeNote: More detail added to the 'how we determine the penalty' and 'representations' sections.

ai.summary: Companies House will enforce the Register of Overseas Entities using its powers, choosing actions based on the failure’s seriousness, impact on individuals or businesses, duration, public interest and any other agency action.
ai.whoAffected: Individuals and businesses that are subject to the Register of Overseas Entities, and the integrity of the registers
actions: Advise clients to ensure all overseas entity information is up‑to‑date and compliant
Monitor any communications from Companies House for enforcement warnings
Document any identified failures and assess their seriousness and duration
Seek professional representation promptly if a penalty or enforcement action is proposed

items.title: Correction slip
items.description: An Act to make provision about finance.

items.title: Companies House approach to non-compliance with mandatory identity verification
items.description: How Companies House will use its enforcement powers in relation to non-compliance with identity verification requirements.

ai.summary: Companies House will monitor and adjust its enforcement approach for mandatory identity verification over time.
ai.whoAffected: Not stated in source

items.title: Budget 2025 document
items.description: This is the full Budget 2025 document in print, web and HTML accessible versions.
items.changeNote: Correction slip added to web and print versions of Budget 2025 document

ai.summary: Not stated in source
ai.whoAffected: Not stated in source

items.title: Budget 2025 speech
items.description: Budget 2025 speech as delivered by Chancellor Rachel Reeves.

ai.summary: The 2025 Budget announces new tax incentives for businesses, a 40% first‑year capital allowance, expanded EMI and EIS/VCT schemes, a three‑year Stamp Duty Reserve Tax exemption for UK listings, and from April 2027 a reformed ISA with £8,000 dedicated to investments.
ai.whoAffected: SMEs, owner‑managed businesses, scale‑up companies, self‑employed entrepreneurs, investors and savers (including over‑65s).
actions: Advise clients on the upcoming ISA change and the £8,000 investment‑only allowance from April 2027
Explain the new 40% first‑year capital allowance and how it can accelerate asset purchases
Review eligibility for expanded Enterprise Management Incentive, Enterprise Investment Scheme and Venture Capital Trust reliefs
Consider the three‑year Stamp Duty Reserve Tax exemption for clients planning a UK listing
legislationRefs: Enterprise Investment and Venture Capital Trust Schemes

items.title: Consultation on the VAT Treatment of Private Hire Vehicles
items.description: Consultation on the potential tax impacts of recent High Court judgments on transport legislation on the private hire vehicle sector and its passengers.

ai.summary: The government is consulting on VAT impacts of two High Court judgments affecting private hire vehicles and passengers, seeking views on possible interventions to reduce adverse effects.
ai.whoAffected: Private hire vehicle operators, drivers, owners and their passengers
actions: Monitor the consultation and its deadlines
Assess how the judgments could affect clients' VAT positions
Gather client input on potential adverse effects
Prepare and submit comments to HMRC on behalf of affected clients
legislationRefs: Uber Britannia Limited v Sefton Borough Council
Uber London Limited v Transport for London

items.title: Reform of Air Passenger Duty for private jets
items.description: This consultation seeks views on reforms to Air Passenger Duty on private jets.

ai.summary: The government is consulting on extending the higher Air Passenger Duty rate to all private jets, including business jets, and reviewing if the weight and passenger‑capacity criteria remain suitable.
ai.whoAffected: Operators and passengers of private jets, including business jets
actions: Monitor the consultation and any forthcoming decisions
Inform clients who own or use private jets about the potential higher APD
Review current APD liabilities for affected clients
Prepare to adjust cost forecasts if the higher rate is applied

items.title: Advance tax certainty for major projects consultation
items.description: This consultation is seeking views on a new process to give major projects increased certainty in advance about the tax that applies.

ai.summary: The government is consulting on a new process to give major projects tax certainty, confirming that Cost Contribution Arrangements can be secured via existing Advance Pricing Agreements, and proposing a revised advance clearance system for R&D reliefs.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses undertaking major projects, firms using Cost Contribution Arrangements, and companies claiming Research & Development reliefs
actions: Monitor the consultation outcomes for major‑project tax certainty
Advise clients on using the existing Advance Pricing Agreement programme for CCAs
Prepare clients for a possible revised advance clearance system for R&D reliefs
Submit client responses to advancetaxcertainty@hmtreasury.gov.uk and advancetaxcertainty@hmrc.gov.uk

items.title: Consultation on the VAT treatment of business donations of goods to charity
items.description: The government is seeking views on the introduction and design of a VAT relief on goods donated to charities to give away free of charge or use in the delivery of their services.

ai.summary: The government is consulting on a new VAT relief for business‑donated goods given to charities for free distribution or service use, aiming to align current rules that only cover charitable sales, while maintaining VAT system security.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses that donate goods to charities and the charities receiving those goods for distribution or service delivery
actions: Monitor the consultation and note key dates
Gather client opinions on potential relief and its impact
Advise clients on current VAT treatment and possible future changes
Prepare briefing material for clients once proposals are finalised

items.title: People with significant control: summary guidance
items.description: This guidance gives an overview of people with significant control (PSC) requirements for companies. If you have a simple ownership and control structure, further guidance may not be needed.

ai.summary: Companies must meet legal duties to identify and record people with significant control (PSCs); non‑compliance can be a criminal offence punishable by fine or imprisonment.
ai.whoAffected: Companies, including SMEs and owner‑managed businesses, and any individuals who qualify as people with significant control
actions: Identify any individuals who meet the PSC criteria for each client company
Maintain an up‑to‑date PSC register as required by law
File PSC information with Companies House within the statutory deadlines
Review compliance regularly to avoid criminal liability

items.description: These Regulations amend the Social Security (Contributions) Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1004) to provide that a payment made to persons under the Post Office Capture Redress Scheme or to nominated individuals is disregarded in the calculation of earnings for the purpose of establishing liability to Class 1 National Insurance Contributions.

items.description: These Regulations amend the Social Security (Contributions) Regulations 2001 (S.I. 2001/1004) to clarify that payments of compensation made under the Horizon Convictions Redress Scheme will be disregarded in the calculation of earnings for the purpose of establishing liability to Class 1 National Insurance Contributions for an expanded group of people eligible under the Scheme. Payments will be ma

items.title: Nine million pensioners to receive Winter Fuel Payments this winter
items.description: Everyone over the State Pension age in England and Wales with an income of, or below, £35,000 a year will benefit from a Winter Fuel Payment this winter.

ai.summary: From winter 2025/26, all pensioners in England and Wales earning £35,000 or less will automatically receive a Winter Fuel Payment (£200 or £300). Those earning above the threshold will have the amount recovered via PAYE or Self‑Assessment, with an opt‑out option.
ai.whoAffected: Pensioners over State Pension age residing in England and Wales – those with taxable income at or below £35,000 are eligible for the payment; those with income above £35,000 will have the payment recovered via tax mechanisms.
actions: Inform pensioner clients that the payment is automatic and no registration is required
Check clients' taxable income to determine if recovery via PAYE or Self‑Assessment will apply
Advise clients on the opt‑out process and any implications for their tax return
Ensure any recovery is correctly reflected in clients' PAYE records or Self‑Assessment filings

items.title: The Finance Act 2021 (Increase in Schedule 26 Penalty Percentages) Regulations 2025
items.description: These Regulations increase the penalties for late payment of tax in Schedule 26 to the Finance Act 2021 (“Schedule 26”).

items.title: The Value Added Tax (Amendment) Regulations 2025
Legislative reform of the Terminal Markets Order: Consultation
items.description: A consultation on legislative reforms to modernise the legislation that underpins the VAT treatment of certain wholesale commodity transactions.

ai.summary: The government proposes to modernise the VAT rules for wholesale commodity trades under the Terminal Markets Order, adding the UK Emissions Trading Scheme and updating post‑EU exit rules for greater certainty.
ai.whoAffected: Businesses that conduct wholesale commodity transactions on named commodity exchanges or market associations (terminal markets), including SMEs, owner‑managed firms and self‑employed traders in that sector
actions: Review which clients trade on terminal markets and assess current VAT treatment
Track the consultation and consider submitting client feedback
Prepare to advise clients on potential VAT changes once the TMO is updated
Update client guidance to include the UK Emissions Trading Scheme within the TMO scope
